FOMC23.verdict: CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT: no event, no zero, no downgrade to DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE; the item is an OUTSTANDING_RELEVANT_ITEM and blocks every cycle until concluded or operator-resolved.

FOMC230.case: HOST SUSPENDS BETWEEN THE WALL READING AND THE COMMIT OF A TRANSACTION

expected.avail: from a response whose request began after the durable commit

FOMC231.case: LATE OLD-EPOCH FEED RESPONSE ARRIVES AFTER A NEWER POLL THAT LISTS A NEW ITEM

expected.late_record: LATE_EVIDENCE, classified after the newer record, no cycle
expected.next_cycle: requires the late record FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL before B

FOMC231.verdict: Late feed evidence is classified fail-safe, never skipped.

FOMC232.case: ITEM LISTED ONLY WHILE EVERY FEED RESPONSE IS CLOCK_UNVERIFIED, THEN DROPPED

expected.candidate: created by classification of the unverified feed

FOMC232.verdict: Clock faults never hide a listing.

FOMC233.case: CONCLUDED OUT-OF-SCOPE ITEM, LATER UNVERIFIED RECHECK SHOWS THE EXACT STATEMENT TITLE

expected.zero: blocked until a LIVE_ELIGIBLE record or RESOLVE

FOMC233.verdict: Ineligible records may reopen, never conclude.

FOMC234.case: QUIET PERIOD: FEED-POLL TASK DIES AFTER TRANSPORT_INVOKED, PROCESS STAYS UP

expected.interrupted: committed at the next periodic tick

FOMC235.case: WALL CLOCK +7 DAYS WHILE O604800 IS PENDING
FOMC235.verdict: Due is decided on server time.

FOMC236.case: HOST REBOOTS EVERY 30 MINUTES DURING A 14400 s BACKOFF

FOMC237.case: LIVE READ AT T BEFORE THE NEWEST RECORD'S OUTCOME COMMITS; LATER REPLAY OF P(T)
FOMC237.verdict: Every snapshot input lies within P(T).

FOMC238.case: NEWEST PRIMARY RECORD CORRUPTED AFTER COMMIT

expected.snapshot: barrier once the integrity diagnostic is in P(T)

FOMC238.verdict: Corruption never makes an older revision current.

FOMC239.case: LATE OLD-EPOCH FEED RECORD WITH THE EXACT TITLE COMMITS AFTER A NEWER FEED THAT RETITLED THE NEW ITEM

expected.order: the newer poll's record (committed first) classifies first; the late record is LATE_EVIDENCE and classifies next

FOMC239.verdict: Classification follows commit order; no sighting is dropped.

FOMC24.case: SUCCESSFUL CYCLE - every listed item KNOWN (concluded) and no outstanding relevant item in the pre-cycle state
FOMC24.verdict: EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO PERMITTED, and explicitly scoped to the V1 capture subset - not to all FOMC monetary-policy activity.

FOMC240.case: TWO STORES: V1 CURRENT VS BARRIER OVER V1 WITH IDENTICAL VISIBLE REVISIONS
FOMC240.verdict: Selection states are part of snapshot identity.

FOMC241.case: ATTEMPT a1 INTERRUPTED AT 600 s WHILE ITS TASK IS ALIVE; a2 COMMITS A CONFLICT; a1's STALE OUT-OF-SCOPE RESPONSE ARRIVES LATER

expected.item: OUTSTANDING (latest LIVE_ELIGIBLE record is the conflict)
expected.snapshot: barrier (newest record unverified, hash differs from the latest verified)

FOMC241.verdict: A late response never concludes an item.

FOMC242.case: CDN SERVES A 200 text/html MAINTENANCE PAGE FOR THE FEED

expected.failed_feed_item: clears at the next LIVE_ELIGIBLE parseable feed

FOMC242.verdict: A malformed feed never stops polling.

FOMC243.case: LIVE READ WHILE EVERY TRANSACTION IS UNRESOLVED AND NO FOMC ITEM IS YET IN THE PREFIX
FOMC243.verdict: An unresolved read is never an empty resolved read.

FOMC244.case: LIVE READ AT T IS FOMC_CAUSAL_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED; THE NEXT VERIFIED POLL LATER RESOLVES THE PREFIX; REPLAY AT (T, H)
FOMC244.verdict: Reads are replayed at their persisted horizon.

FOMC245.case: NEWEST FEED RECORD IN P(T) HAS NO CONCLUSION YET; AN OLDER CYCLE CONCLUDED ZERO
FOMC245.verdict: An older zero is never presented as current.

FOMC246.verdict: A return seen only through backfill is never LIVE-available.

FOMC25.case: POSITIVE FEED CANDIDATE, PRIMARY FETCH FAILS
FOMC25.verdict: no normalized event; the acquisition stays under retry_policy (possibly SUSPENDED); SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on primary_statement; the item is outstanding, so every cycle is NOT_ZERO until it concludes or an operator resolves it.

FOMC26.case: OFFICIAL DATE CORRECTION ON SAME URL - R3/X6
FOMC26.preconditions: same P, E and U; H1 != H2; D1 != D2; both observations satisfy the existing normalization requirements
FOMC26.same_body_control: identical verified primary body bytes under the SAME CaptureSpec hash MUST yield the same official_statement_date. A different date is a PARSER/NORMALIZER DETERMINISM FAILURE: FAIL CLOSED, no new content revision, no normalized overwrite.
FOMC26.verdict: SAME source_item_id S; append R2 with D2; retain R1 with D1 unchanged. Date correction alone is NOT an identity conflict. No duplicate logical event, no overwrite, no retroactive visibility mutation. Both revisions retain source_available_at = null and source_updated_at = null, with their own observed_at and ingested_at.
FOMC26.with_guid: same GUID on both observations: SAME S, R2 appended; existing GUID conflicts still fail closed if independently triggered
FOMC26.without_guid: historical archive/backfill, no RSS GUID on either observation: SAME S, R2 appended; GUID absence does not alter identity

FOMC27.preconditions: U1 is extracted from a durable official feed/archive artifact and passes existing validation; U1 -> U2 satisfies existing redirect security rules
FOMC27.verdict: canonical_primary_statement_url = normalize(U1) using existing url_canonicalization; source_item_id derives from that value. U2 and the redirect chain are transport provenance only. NEVER re-key from normalize(U2). Computing identity does not bypass existing primary classification or revision-admission requirements.

FOMC28.changed_body: append a NEW immutable content revision under SAME S according to existing revision_policy
FOMC28.preconditions: same provider_id and event_family; same normalized official discovery URL; both redirect chains pass existing security rules
FOMC28.same_body: SAME content revision; transport movement alone creates no content revision
FOMC28.verdict: U1 -> U2 then U1 -> U3 keeps canonical_primary_statement_url = normalize(U1) and source_item_id = S. Record differing transport provenance. No new logical item and no identity conflict solely from the redirect-topology change; existing independent GUID conflicts still apply.

FOMC29.verdict: a primary-page <link rel="canonical" href="U4"> has NO semantic or identity authority in V1. Identity remains normalize(U1); no replacement, merge, split, re-key or identity conflict solely because U4 differs. If retained, U4 is optional non-authoritative diagnostic/provenance only.

FOMC30.verdict: U1 comes from a durable validated backfill manifest entry, passes existing validation and normalization, and anchors source_item_id before U1 -> U2. No GUID required; no identity from U2, HTML canonical or a synthetic date-derived URL. Backfill observations create no reobservation grid.

FOMC31.preconditions: same provider_id and event_family; only the ASCII scheme casing differs; existing official-discovery and non-scheme URL validation requirements hold
FOMC31.verdict: ACCEPT HTTPS scheme using ASCII case-insensitive comparison; serialize exactly lowercase ASCII https in canonical_primary_statement_url. Every listed scheme spelling yields expected_identity_url and the SAME source_item_id. Original spelling remains in durable raw discovery provenance only. Scheme case alone causes no new source item, identity conflict or content revision; all existing primary admission requirements still apply.

FOMC32.verdict: REJECT at scheme admission. NEVER silently upgrade http to https. No canonical identity URL, no source_item_id admission and no primary request. ftp, file, data, javascript and an empty/missing scheme are also rejected under scheme_admission.

FOMC33.preconditions: same provider_id and event_family; only explicit default-port presence differs; all other existing official-discovery and URL validation requirements hold
FOMC33.verdict: ACCEPT both absent port and explicit decimal 443, then OMIT the port component from canonical_primary_statement_url. The identity URLs are byte-identical and yield the SAME source_item_id. Explicit default-port presence alone creates no source item, identity conflict or content revision. Original :443 spelling remains in durable raw discovery provenance only; existing primary admission requirements still apply.

FOMC34.verdict: REJECT before source_item_id derivation/admission and before any primary request. NEVER strip :444 and continue or rewrite it to :443. Every other explicit non-443 port and every malformed explicit port fails closed under port_admission; no custom-port exception.

FOMC35.verdict: REJECT: the literal % does not begin % HEXDIG HEXDIG. No canonical_primary_statement_url or source_item_id is admitted and no primary request occurs. Do not preserve the malformed percent as a literal fallback or repair it. The durable discovery artifact retains the original source text unchanged.

FOMC36.verdict: REJECT: %2 has only one following ASCII hex digit. No identity derivation/admission or request; never guess the missing nibble or decode a partial escape. Existing component restrictions also remain mandatory.

FOMC37.verdict: REJECT: G is not an ASCII hex digit. No identity derivation/admission or request. The same URL used as a redirect target MUST be rejected before follow. Do not repair, change case and retry, or treat % literally. Existing redirect identity and security rules otherwise remain unchanged.

FOMC38.full_url_admission: NOT ASSERTED - this case tests percent syntax only; all other existing V1 component and primary-path restrictions still apply
FOMC38.verdict: PASS this syntax gate: %2F consists of % and two ASCII hex digits. This gate leaves the path unchanged under existing V1 path-preservation semantics; it MUST NOT decode %2F into /. No identity or request admission is implied by syntax success alone, and no equivalence with / or %2f is decided by FIX7.

FOMC39.case: COMPRESSION BOMB / DECODED BODY OVER LIMIT
FOMC39.verdict: ABORT during bounded decoded-body production as soon as output would exceed 5242880 bytes. Do not append excess bytes, finish decompression to measure 20 MiB, or invoke text decoding/parsing/normalization. No complete accepted body artifact or successful complete-body hash may be created from the incomplete prefix. Existing oversized-body PARSER_FAILED mapping applies; EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO is forbidden.

FOMC40.verdict: A complete decoded body of exactly the configured limit passes ONLY the size gate; all other existing admission/parsing rules still apply. One additional decoded byte aborts body decoding at attempted excess, before text decoding or parsing, under the same PARSER_FAILED and no-artifact/hash/revision rules as FOMC39. MiB means 1048576 bytes, not decimal MB.

FOMC41.verdict: REJECT under text_decoding_v1: the HTTP declaration is unsupported and incompatible with the HTML declaration. No authority competition, windows-1252 decoding of E9 as e-acute, fallback or EventRevision. The strict UTF-8 default cannot override an incompatible signal.

FOMC42.verdict: PASS text decoding as strict UTF-8 using the explicit V1 default, with no BOM or recognized meta declaration. This is not charset detection or fallback. Other existing parsing/admission checks remain mandatory; a text-decoding pass alone does not admit an EventRevision.

FOMC43.other_signals: absent or all UTF-8-compatible; remaining body is valid UTF-8
FOMC43.verdict: PASS text decoding. Consume exactly one leading EF BB BF as an encoding signature for the text view only; do not expose that signature as a leading U+FEFF. The persisted/hash/replay bytes still include the original BOM. No stripping of additional body code points or new Unicode normalization.

FOMC44.verdict: REJECT the unsupported XML encoding declaration even if the body happens to contain only valid UTF-8/ASCII bytes. Do not select ISO-8859-1, ignore the declaration or retry another decoder.

FOMC45.declaration_source: HTTP charset or any recognized XML/HTML encoding declaration
FOMC45.verdict: REJECT because x-unknown is not one of utf-8 or utf8 after the frozen label normalization. No platform codec/alias lookup, heuristic detection or fallback.

FOMC46.verdict: REJECT invalid UTF-8 under STRICT decoding. No errors=ignore, errors=replace, surrogateescape, codec guessing or fallback. Previously admitted raw bytes and their byte hash remain unchanged; no EventRevision or zero from this failed response.

FOMC47.verdict: PASS strict UTF-8 text decoding: HTTP, BOM and HTML meta all agree. Consume the single leading signature only in the text view. No first-wins/last-wins choice, alternate decoder or automatic EventRevision admission.

FOMC48.case: DOCUMENT TITLE IS NON-AUTHORITATIVE - document <title> reads "Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement" and an inline SVG <title>Lock</title> is also present; h3.title reads "Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement"
FOMC48.verdict: primary-page-title predicate MATCHES on the authoritative h3.title. Both <title> elements are ignored for classifier authority; the prefixed document title cannot cause a mismatch and the SVG title cannot interfere.

FOMC49.case: DUPLICATE TITLE ANCHOR - two h3.title nodes inside the authoritative region
FOMC49.verdict: PARSER_FAILED. No first/last/visible wins. No EventRevision. EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO blocked.

FOMC50.case: DUPLICATE RELEASE ELEMENT - two p.releaseTime start elements inside the authoritative region
FOMC50.verdict: PARSER_FAILED even if their text is identical. No first-match behaviour. No EventRevision. Zero blocked.

FOMC51.case: MISSING REQUIRED ANCHOR - title or date anchor absent while the page is otherwise syntactically valid (an absent release-line anchor is FOMC158's non-gating case)
FOMC51.verdict: PARSER_FAILED. No fallback to document metadata, whole-page text or any node outside the frozen region.

FOMC52.case: ENTITY THEN NFC - authoritative text contains the semantic equivalent of "é"
FOMC52.verdict: character-reference resolution yields U+0065 U+0301, then NFC yields the canonical composed form where applicable. NFC-first is forbidden, so the outcome is order-independent only because the order is frozen.

FOMC53.verdict: semantic text before comparison is A U+00A0 B. NBSP is not in the ASCII whitespace set and is NOT collapsed to U+0020. No browser-layout equivalence.

FOMC54.case:
UNCLOSED RELEASE PARAGRAPH -

holds the release declaration, is never closed, and is followed by

    then the share menu and statement body
FOMC54.verdict: release_line_source_text is ONLY the leading character data before <ul>. Normalized result is exactly the release declaration; no share-menu or body text is admitted. The parser DOM recovery strategy cannot alter this result. This is the real observed template on 5/5 evidence pages.

FOMC55.case: EMPTY RELEASE LEADING TEXT - unique p.releaseTime exists but the next markup token arrives before any non-whitespace semantic character data
FOMC55.verdict: PARSER_FAILED. No descendant or global fallback.

FOMC56.case: LAST UPDATE SAME VALUE AS OFFICIAL DATE - p.article__time reads "January 28, 2026" and div#lastUpdate reads "Last Update: January 28, 2026"
FOMC56.verdict: official_statement_date comes ONLY from p.article__time. An equal displayed value can never make div#lastUpdate authoritative - the distinction is structural, which is exactly why a value check would have failed to separate them on all 5 evidence samples.

FOMC57.case: INTERNAL ENTITY BOMB - a feed body far below 2 MiB carrying <!DOCTYPE rss [ <!ENTITY a "lol"> <!ENTITY b "&a;&a;..."> ... ]> with nested internal entity declarations
FOMC57.verdict: PARSER_FAILED at the forbidden-DOCTYPE security gate. No entity expansion occurs, no semantic feed parse happens, and EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO is blocked. The 2 MiB input cap is satisfied and irrelevant - the DOCTYPE prohibition is what stops it.

FOMC58.case: EXTERNAL GENERAL ENTITY - <!DOCTYPE rss [ <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> ]> with &xxe; in the body
FOMC58.verdict: PARSER_FAILED. No filesystem read, no substituted text, no zero. Rejection precedes any resource access.

FOMC59.case: EXTERNAL PARAMETER ENTITY / EXTERNAL DTD CHAIN - an external parameter entity or external DTD reference
FOMC59.verdict: PARSER_FAILED. No network, no local file access, no resolver invocation, no zero.

FOMC60.verdict: PARSER_FAILED. No fetch and no include processing. Not treated as an inert unknown element, because that would be library-dependent.

FOMC61.case: BUILT-IN XML ENTITY REFERENCES - valid feed content containing & < > ' "
FOMC61.verdict: NOT rejected by FIX11. These are built-in XML references, not custom DTD entity declarations; normal XML semantics continue. Numeric character references likewise remain permitted.

FOMC62.case: DOCTYPE-LIKE TEXT IN A COMMENT - "<!-- <!DOCTYPE rss [ ... ]> -->" with no actual DOCTYPE declaration
FOMC62.verdict: NOT rejected. The security gate is syntax-aware, so a character sequence inside comment text is not a prohibited construct. This case exists specifically to prove the policy is not naive substring matching.

FOMC63.case: 404 WITH VALID-LOOKING STATEMENT BODY - status 404, body is valid UTF-8 with correct anchors, the exact title and a valid release line
FOMC63.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No HTML semantic parse, no EventRevision, no zero. Body appearance cannot override status.

FOMC64.case: 500 WITH VALID-LOOKING RSS - status 500, body is well-formed valid-looking Fed RSS
FOMC64.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No semantic feed success and no EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO.

FOMC65.case: 206 PARTIAL CONTENT - status 206, body is a syntactically valid partial statement
FOMC65.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No content admission, no successful body hash, no EventRevision. This is the server-declared counterpart to the client-side truncation FIX8 already forbade.

FOMC66.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No accepted empty body, no hash, no revision, no zero.

FOMC67.case: 304 WITHOUT PRIOR BODY - status 304 and no verified prior body exists
FOMC67.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No body reuse, no synthesized body, no revision.

FOMC68.case: 304 WITH VERIFIED PRIOR BODY - status 304 while a verified prior complete body exists locally
FOMC68.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE anyway. V1 conditional caching and reuse remain unsupported. The prior body remains historical local data and is NOT substituted into this HTTP observation; no new EventRevision is caused by a 304.

FOMC69.case: VALID REDIRECT CHAIN TO 200 - initial 302, then 301, then final 200, all targets valid on the allowed host
FOMC69.verdict: the allowed transitions are followed and the final 200 body may enter the normal pipeline. Logical identity remains the original official discovery URL; the final URL is non-identifying provenance.

FOMC70.case: FOURTH REDIRECT - the chain produces four redirect responses
FOMC70.verdict: the first three transitions may be followed. When the response after redirect #3 is itself a redirect, that fourth target is NOT requested. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, no semantic body admission.

FOMC71.case: REDIRECT WITHOUT LOCATION - an allowed redirect status such as 302 with no Location header
FOMC71.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. The target is never guessed or reconstructed.

FOMC72.case: CACHE VALIDATOR IS NON-CAUSAL - a response carries ETag and Last-Modified
FOMC72.verdict: both may be persisted as HTTP provenance. Neither may set source_available_at, source_updated_at, declared_release_at, observed_at or ingested_at, and no content-vintage inference may be drawn.

FOMC73.verdict: resolved candidate https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/c.htm; after full V1 validation it MAY be followed. Explicitly supported.

FOMC74.verdict: path merging and dot-segment removal yield https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/b.htm, then normal validation. Explicitly supported.

FOMC75.case: SCHEME-RELATIVE SAME HOST - Location: //www.federalreserve.gov/foo.htm over a current https URL
FOMC75.verdict: network-path reference inherits scheme https, giving https://www.federalreserve.gov/foo.htm, then normal validation. Explicitly supported.

FOMC76.verdict: resolves to https://evil.example/foo.htm, then the host allowlist REJECTS it BEFORE any request. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; the host is never contacted. Resolution does not grant trust.

FOMC77.case: EMPTY LOCATION - header present but empty, or only SP/HTAB
FOMC77.verdict: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE after outer-OWS trimming. No same-URL inference, no resolution against the base, no request.

FOMC78.verdict: resolve FIRST to https://www.federalreserve.gov/foo.htm?x=1, THEN the unchanged V1 query prohibition rejects it. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, no request. The query is NEVER silently stripped to make the target admissible.

FOMC79.verdict: resolves to the current absolute resource plus fragment; the existing fragment-removal rule then makes the effective request resource equal the current one. It is still a redirect transition, so FIX12's max-three limit terminates any loop. Identity unchanged. A fragment-only Location is NOT treated as missing.

FOMC80.verdict: admission fails before any request under the unchanged FIX7 percent gate. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

FOMC81.verdict: the absolute reference resolves as HTTP and the existing HTTPS-required rule rejects it. No auto-upgrade to HTTPS, no request. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

FOMC82.case: BASE ADVANCES PER HOP - U0 https://www.federalreserve.gov/a/one.htm, L1 ../b/two.htm -> U1 https://www.federalreserve.gov/b/two.htm; U1 returns Location: three.htm
FOMC82.verdict: U2 is https://www.federalreserve.gov/b/three.htm, NOT https://www.federalreserve.gov/a/three.htm. This proves each Location resolves against the CURRENT requested hop URL rather than the original U0.

FOMC83.case: THREE-REQUEST REDIRECT CHAIN - GET U0 -> 302; GET U1 -> 301; GET U2 -> 200
FOMC83.verdict: Three physical attempts, not one logical-fetch unit. U0, U1 and U2 each pass through the SAME provider gate before network side effects; final 200 admission and pre-redirect identity remain unchanged.

FOMC84.case: MAXIMAL REDIRECT CHAIN - initial U0 plus three followed transitions to U1, U2 and U3; U3 may return redirect #4 to U4
FOMC84.verdict: Four actually attempted GETs consume four units through the shared gate. If U3 proposes redirect #4, FIX12 forbids requesting U4: no fifth attempt or unit, existing SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE outcome unchanged.

FOMC85.case: FEED THEN PRIMARY - one successful feed GET discovers one item; one primary GET follows later
FOMC85.verdict: One feed attempt plus one primary attempt consume two units in the SAME provider domain; never one combined unit or independent feed/primary quotas.

FOMC86.case: REDIRECT TARGET REJECTED BEFORE REQUEST - U0 returns 302 Location: //evil.example/x
FOMC86.verdict: U0 consumed one unit. FIX13 resolves then rejects the foreign host before contact: no physical attempt for the rejected target, no additional unit. Existing redirect rejection outcome remains unchanged.

FOMC87.case: FAILED ATTEMPT STILL COUNTS - permission to begin a provider attempt is granted; DNS/connect/TLS/transport subsequently fails
FOMC87.verdict: The admitted start consumed one unit before network side effects, even without a successful response. No refund and no successful SourceObservation or EventRevision implied; existing failure mapping applies.

FOMC88.case: PERMITTED LATER REATTEMPT - an earlier attempt fails; existing retry policy later permits another attempt through normal scheduling
FOMC88.verdict: The first failure does not refund its unit. The separately permitted later attempt reacquires the same provider gate and consumes another unit. No free retry, new retry permission, hidden library retry or tight loop.

FOMC89.case: RECHECK SHARES PROVIDER BUDGET - feed/primary traffic and one scheduled revision recheck are pending
FOMC89.verdict: The recheck shares the SAME accounting domain as feed and primary traffic. It cannot start without provider permission even when due; each actually attempted GET consumes one unit. Ordering is frozen by revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.selection (FOMC126); the first-successful-primary anchor and offsets are unchanged.

FOMC90.preconditions: rate_limiter.boundary_examples.time_origin: exclusive ownership and startup embargo already satisfied; t=0 is not epoch begin.
FOMC90.verdict: Start 0 has age exactly 60 and is outside (t-60s,t). Five prior starts remain; adding candidate 60 gives six in (t-60s,t]. Exact 10-second spacing passes: ADMITTED. The sequence 0,10,20,30,40,50,60 is valid.

FOMC91.preconditions: Epoch ownership/embargo already satisfied as in rate_limiter.boundary_examples.time_origin.
FOMC91.verdict: WAIT: start 0 is still active because age <60; all six prior starts count. Spacing from 50 is also <10. No physical start or consumed unit.

FOMC92.verdict: Exact equality passes START_TO_START spacing. Actual admission additionally requires window and ownership/epoch preconditions; equality grants no exemption from those gates.

FOMC93.case: SLOW PREVIOUS RESPONSE - A starts 0, completes 45; B candidate 45
FOMC93.preconditions: t=0 is a post-embargo origin as in rate_limiter.boundary_examples.time_origin.
FOMC93.verdict: B may start at 45 if the rolling window and ownership preconditions permit. No completion +10 wait to 55. Spacing uses the previous START event only.

FOMC94.case: WALL CLOCK JUMPS BACKWARD - monotonic previous start 100, candidate 105; UTC jumps backward five minutes
FOMC94.verdict: WAIT: monotonic delta remains 5, so spacing fails. UTC changes neither window history nor spacing/embargo comparisons; normal UTC provenance is preserved.

FOMC95.case: TWO SIMULTANEOUS WORKERS - five active prior starts; spacing and ownership/embargo otherwise permit; A and B request the same instant
FOMC95.verdict: One candidate may be granted first; its registration is atomic with consumption. The other must re-evaluate updated provider history and fails spacing at the same instant. The winner is not prescribed; fairness/order are not part of this fix.

FOMC96.case: CANCEL AFTER GRANT - one atomic slot is consumed at t, then task cancels before any network side effect
FOMC96.verdict: The t grant remains in both histories under normal age rules. No refund or reuse; a future attempt needs fresh admission. No successful SourceObservation or EventRevision is implied.

FOMC97.case: RESTART EMBARGO - new exclusive limiter epoch begins e=0 with no current-epoch starts
FOMC97.preconditions: Old independent issuers cannot initiate more provider attempts; e measures elapsed time since the new epoch begins under exclusive ownership.
FOMC97.verdict: No starts before 60; exact 60 passes embargo and normal gates are then evaluated on empty new-epoch history. No prior monotonic timestamp comparison or UTC fast path.

FOMC98.case: FEED THEN PRIMARY TOO QUICKLY - feed starts 100, primary candidate 101
FOMC98.verdict: WAIT. Feed and primary share the same limiter; primary is spacing-eligible no earlier than 110, subject also to the rolling window and ownership/epoch gates.

FOMC99.case: IMMEDIATE REDIRECT FOLLOW - U0 starts 200, returns 302 at 201, validated redirect target candidate at 201
FOMC99.verdict: WAIT. Redirect follow must reacquire the same provider limiter; earliest spacing eligibility is 210, subject also to the rolling window. HTTP auto-follow cannot bypass admission.

binds.design_overrides: for FOMC items this spec overrides design rev4 revision_policy.selection and extends snapshot_identity.binds (snapshot_binding), overrides durability_and_transaction_policy.ingested_at_assignment (ingested_at is the server-attested avail of the committing transaction, causal_predicates.avail) and replaces per-revision gating timestamps with revision_policy.revision_mode_neutrality: a revision is keyed by (source item, content hash) and its availability through each observation is carried by that observation's link; design RevisionId derivation from gating timestamps does not apply. All other design rules apply
binds.shared_http_primitive: scripts/trading_lab/safe_http.py::require_https_host ONLY (scheme, userinfo, host and port checks), reused as one of the V1 URL checks

shared_http_primitive_conformance.AllowlistedRedirectHandler: NOT CONFORMING for FOMC V1 - it inherits urllib automatic redirect following (up to 10 redirects inside one urlopen, URI header fallback, unbounded redirect-body read, single timeout, no per-hop limiter grant or deadline)
shared_http_primitive_conformance.build_hardened_opener: NOT CONFORMING for FOMC V1 for the same reason
shared_http_primitive_conformance.implementation_status: No existing repo primitive implements http_policy.redirect_implementation. Phase 6G-A must supply one; this spec does not claim existing code conforms.
shared_http_primitive_conformance.require_https_host: REUSED as a necessary, NOT sufficient, check. It accepts inputs V1 rejects (empty port ':', stripped control characters, leading whitespace) and can raise a bare ValueError; url_canonicalization port admission, whitespace/control-character and malformed-authority rules are checked separately, and any exception is a rejection.

canonical_serialization.generated_at_field: deliberately absent so the spec hash is reproducible
canonical_serialization.rule: json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8'), SHA-256 over those bytes

causal_predicates.LIVE_ELIGIBLE: the single causal predicate: a per-response record R is LIVE_ELIGIBLE iff R is PROCESSABLE, CLOCK_VERIFIED (its own Date/Age, reference age 0), of observation_mode LIVE (including MANUAL_RETRY of LIVE work), and not LATE_EVIDENCE. It is fixed at commit and never changes. It alone governs LIVE causal state: reobservation anchor creation, discovery-cycle causal admission, obligation satisfaction, episode success, natural item conclusion and LIVE availability evidence. It never gates local processing.
causal_predicates.PROCESSABLE: fixed at commit: a per-response record is PROCESSABLE iff it is an admitted complete final-200 response whose raw bytes, digest and required metadata commit in its own transaction. Every PROCESSABLE record is processed to a terminal local outcome (RECORD_PROCESSING_TERMINAL) whatever its clock verdict or mode; clock evidence never blocks parsing, classification, health recording or processing. Integrity loss detected later never changes PROCESSABLE: it yields CORRUPTION_FAIL_CLOSED if no outcome exists yet, an integrity diagnostic, and a snapshot barrier (snapshot_binding.algorithm).
causal_predicates.SERVER_NOW_LB: NOW_LB(store) = max over CLOCK_VERIFIED per-response records other than LATE_EVIDENCE of (observed_at - 92); it is <= the true current instant under the assumption below, is monotone in the store, survives restarts, boots, suspend and VM pauses, and advances with every verified response (normally each feed poll). It is the only time scale for due and backoff decisions; feed cadence and local deadlines are liveness timers on monotonic/boottime.
causal_predicates.assumption: the provider's Date + Age is its serve instant truncated to whole seconds (a compliant origin or cache). Residuals, both requiring coincident provider and host clock faults: (1) a server whose Date lags true time by L > 2 s, observed by a collector whose clock is more than 92 s slow and within 90 s of that lagging Date, can make visibility early by at most L - 2 s; (2) a server and collector both wrong forward by F advance NOW_LB and every later avail by up to F, since both are maxima over an append-only store: pending obligations may become due early and, until true time catches up, FOMC visibility and backoff-gated retries wait; provider traffic stays within the 120 bound.

avail.CAUSALLY_ADMISSIBLE_BOUNDED: a PROCESSABLE CLOCK_VERIFIED record whose transaction avail is resolved; the only kind of causal admissibility in V1. A record whose transaction is never resolved stays EVIDENCE_ONLY forever
avail.never_rewritten: commit_seq, raw records and original observed_at are never rewritten; avail is derived evidence only
avail.rule: avail(X) = max(V.observed_at + 92, every observed_at concerned by X's records, avail of every earlier transaction), where V is the first (by its own commit_seq) CLOCK_VERIFIED per-response record other than LATE_EVIDENCE whose TRANSPORT_INVOKED has commit_seq > X.commit_seq. V's request was sent after X was durable, so its true serve instant (< V.observed_at + 92) is later than X's durability. X is UNRESOLVED until V exists.
avail.uniform: the rule applies to every transaction; no local reading other than a verified observed_at (itself bounded by the server's Date/Age) enters availability, so pauses, suspend, slow commits and wall steps cannot make anything available early

constants.CLOCK_ERROR_BOUND_S: 92 = 90 + 2, the only tolerance any causal rule uses. Derivation: for a CLOCK_VERIFIED response R with true serve instant s, Date + Age <= s < Date + Age + 2, and |observed_at - (Date + Age)| <= 90, hence s - 92 < observed_at <= s + 90, so s is within [observed_at - 90, observed_at + 92) and within 92 s of observed_at either way
constants.CLOCK_REFERENCE_MAX_AGE_S: 0: a record is LIVE_ELIGIBLE only on its own server-verified clock evidence; no record inherits clock trust from another, so no elapsed-time clock (monotonic or boottime, which a VM pause can freeze) enters any causal rule. This is the smallest possible value and needs no grace period.
constants.DATE_AGE_GRANULARITY_S: 2: Date and Age are whole seconds, each truncated by < 1 s

causal_predicates.production_requirement: an NTP-disciplined host; NTP is defense in depth, never proof
causal_predicates.replay: every predicate and avail is recomputed from persisted Date/Age lines, observed_at, verdicts and commit_seq; mismatch or missing input fails replay closed

dom_anchor_evidence.not_a_provider_contract: the Federal Reserve publishes no markup contract. These anchors are empirical observations across the evidence sample, not a guaranteed API.
dom_anchor_evidence.role: DESIGN/SPEC PROVENANCE ONLY. This hash explains why the anchors below were frozen. It is NOT an identity input: no runtime identity component is created from it, and source_item_id is unchanged.

durable_ordering.basis: design rev4 durability_and_transaction_policy: a single authoritative SQLite EventStore with serialized write transactions; store commit order disambiguates STORAGE chronology and never overrides semantic source-time rules

commit_instant.ingested_at: for an EventRevision and an observation-to-revision link, ingested_at = avail of its transaction (null while UNRESOLVED); never earlier than any observed_at concerned
commit_instant.latency: a transaction resolves at the next verified response whose request starts after it; with an accurate clock it becomes visible about 150-250 s after commit (next poll, fetch time, + 92 s); until then it is UNRESOLVED and visibility waits
commit_instant.one_record_per_transaction: each per-response record, each attempt record and each processing outcome commits in its own transaction
commit_instant.ordering: commit_seq is the only ordering; nothing is reordered, re-stamped or moved
commit_instant.provenance_readings: each transaction persists wall_at_commit as provenance only; it never affects availability
commit_instant.rule: causal_predicates.avail; every transaction commits regardless of clock state, so capture never stalls on clock uncertainty

durable_ordering.late_durable_record: A per-response record that commits after a limiter-epoch transition is its attempt's outcome only while that attempt has no outcome; otherwise it is LATE_EVIDENCE (retry_policy.attempt_outcome_fence). Either way it receives a larger commit_seq, is considered identically by live derivation and replay, and can never displace an anchor or revision chosen from a smaller commit_seq.
durable_ordering.not_business_truth: commit_seq never replaces observed_at, ingested_at, due_at or any causal timestamp and is never an identity input
durable_ordering.rule: Every durable record this spec relies on (per-response raw/observation record, EPISODE_OPEN, TRANSPORT_INVOKED, attempt outcome, EPISODE_SUCCEEDED/SUSPENDED record, processing outcome record, observation-to-revision link, operator record, snapshot watermark, feed item conclusion, cycle conclusion, EventRevision, manifest, operator retry request) carries commit_seq: the strictly increasing position of its committing transaction in the authoritative store. commit_seq is assigned inside the committing transaction and exists only if that transaction commits.
uses: 'first'/'earliest'/'latest'/'before' between durable records ALWAYS means commit_seq order unless a rule explicitly names a timestamp comparison
reobservation anchor selection (the LIVE_ELIGIBLE record with the smallest commit_seq)
EventRevision source observation selection (the qualifying record carrying H with the smallest commit_seq)
zero pre-cycle state (records with commit_seq smaller than the cycle's feed record)

cache_validators.fix1_consistency: these validators cannot retroproject a later-fetched body; this is the same prohibition FIX1 froze for Last Update

http_date.note: never content-vintage proof and never a replacement for observed_at; the final response's Date/Age are the per-response clock-check input and, through observed_at, the server-attested time scale (causal_predicates)

cache_validators.may_be_retained_as: exact HTTP provenance/diagnostic metadata under existing provenance semantics
must_never_become: a request-decision input in V1, except through NOW_LB (causal_predicates.SERVER_NOW_LB), which only delays due and backoff decisions

conditional_requests.rule: FOMC V1 MUST NOT send If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since, so normal compliant operation never depends on receiving a 304. If an upstream or proxy nevertheless produces one, the 304 policy applies: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
conditional_requests.superseded_wording: rev12 said only "V1 CORRECTNESS MUST NOT DEPEND ON HTTP 304", which never stated what happens IF a 304 arrives. That gap is now closed.

content_type_gate.charset: a charset parameter must satisfy parser_policy.text_decoding_v1.http_charset_policy (UTF-8 compatible); otherwise PARSER_FAILED
content_type_gate.comparison: type/subtype compared ASCII case-insensitively; parameter names ASCII case-insensitive; parameter order irrelevant; after the duplicate check, parameters other than charset do not affect admission
content_type_gate.duplicate_parameter_name: any parameter name appearing twice within one value (case-insensitively) -> PARSER_FAILED
content_type_gate.field_name: Content-Type header field name matched ASCII case-insensitively
content_type_gate.header_absence_note: text_decoding_v1's recorded-header-absence input remains provenance only; an admitted body can never reach text decoding without passing this gate
content_type_gate.missing: no Content-Type field -> PARSER_FAILED; no sniffing
content_type_gate.multiple_values: each Content-Type field line is one value; if every value parses, all share the same case-folded type/subtype and each passes parser_policy.text_decoding_v1.http_charset_policy, the gate passes; otherwise PARSER_FAILED
content_type_gate.quoted_string: quoted-pairs are unescaped per RFC 9110 before the charset label is evaluated
content_type_gate.stage: after durable raw persistence (raw retained), before charset/text decoding
content_type_gate.unparseable_value: PARSER_FAILED (including an unquoted comma, empty value or missing subtype)
content_type_gate.value_grammar: OWS type '/' subtype *( OWS ';' OWS [ parameter ] ) OWS (RFC 9110): empty parameters and a trailing ';' are allowed; type, subtype and parameter names are tokens; a parameter value is a token or quoted-string

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.accepted_buffer_rule: Start decoded_count at 0. For each incrementally produced decoded chunk, before appending, if decoded_count + len(chunk) > the applicable body limit, ABORT immediately without appending excess bytes. Otherwise append and increment decoded_count. The accepted decoded-body accumulation MUST never exceed the applicable cap.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.basis: UNCHANGED raw_policy.bytes_semantics: HTTP entity-body bytes after all applicable transport/content decoding required by the frozen body-byte semantics, before any charset/text decoding. This rule changes WHEN the existing decoded-body limit is enforced, not the hashed/persisted/replay byte stage.

content_length_role.missing_or_misleading_value: The same decoded-body cap and incremental enforcement remain mandatory, including when Content-Length is absent, incorrect or smaller than decoded output.
content_length_role.permitted_role: Transport provenance or an early rejection hint only as already permitted by existing semantics; never a substitute for decoded-byte counting. Compressed-byte length and socket-byte length are not the decoded-size authority either.

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.decoded_output_production: Decoder output production itself MUST be incrementally bounded while enforcing the applicable decoded-body cap. Checking chunks after an unbounded decoding call has already materialized the complete expansion is NOT conforming. Stop decoding immediately when further output would exceed the cap; do not continue consuming/decompressing the remainder merely to determine final size.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.encoding_scope: The same cap applies to identity, gzip, brotli or any other encoding ONLY insofar as it is already admitted by frozen V1 semantics. FIX8 adds no encoding support. A small compressed representation cannot bypass the decoded-body limit.

limit_boundary.pass_scope: Size gate only; successful complete-body admission still requires every other existing V1 check.

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.memory_guarantee_scope: The accepted decoded-body accumulation is bounded by the configured cap and decoded output production must stop at attempted excess. No total process-memory, constant-memory, exact RSS or decompressor-internal-memory guarantee is claimed. Library, chunk size, buffer layout and bounded decoding API are implementation choices; unbounded decompress-all followed by a size check is not.

oversized_body.partial_body_replay: FORBIDDEN - no incomplete prefix may be treated as a complete response, hashed as a normal successful complete body, or replayed/parsed as one. This fix introduces no partial-body replay or diagnostic hash semantics.
oversized_body.provenance: Retain transport/provenance and failure metadata only as already permitted by the existing design. An oversized decoded response MUST NOT be persisted or admitted as a valid complete raw body artifact.
oversized_body.source_health_binding: Reuse source_health.mappings['decoded body exceeds the frozen size bound']; no new global health state. Oversize is terminal for this response's normal capture pipeline.

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.pipeline_gate: An oversized response MUST NOT reach charset/text decoding, an XML parser, an HTML parser or the normalizer. No truncation-and-continue, parse-first-N-MiB or best effort.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.raw_replay_preservation: For complete admitted bodies, existing hash bytes, persisted body bytes and offline replay input bytes remain unchanged. Raw-first persistence before parsing remains mandatory; no successful complete-body SHA-256 is manufactured from an aborted prefix.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.redirect_scope: Applies where an HTTP body is consumed under existing V1 policy. Redirect identity, validation and follow rules are unchanged; this fix introduces no redirect-body parsing semantics.

http_status_policy.body_appearance_cannot_override_status: a 404 body containing perfectly valid-looking FOMC HTML is SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with no HTML semantic parse, no event and no zero. A 500 body containing well-formed valid-looking Fed RSS is SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with no feed success and no EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO.

covers_non_exhaustively: 3xx not successfully followed as an intermediate redirect

final_body_admission.rule: a final HTTP response body is eligible for NORMAL FOMC V1 content processing IF AND ONLY IF final_status_code == 200, by EXACT equality. NOT any 2xx, NOT status < 400, NOT "a body is present", NOT "the body looks valid".

http_status_policy.fix12_non_scope: FIX12 does NOT decide whether a 429, 500, 503 or timeout is retried - it only freezes that if such a response is the FINAL response of the logical attempt, it is non-admitted and maps to SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Existing polling.retry_policy remains authoritative and unchanged. FIX14 binds redirect and permitted later reattempt accounting to request_accounting; FIX15 rate_limiter defines their shared temporal admission, without changing retry permissions or response admission.
gate_order: 2. record allowed transport/provenance metadata under existing semantics
3. classify the response as an intermediate allowed redirect, a final exact 200, or a non-admitted final/error response
4. ONLY a final exact 200 may enter normal complete-body acquisition, decoded-size enforcement, durable-body persistence, content hashing, text decoding and semantic parsing

no_content.rule: no accepted empty body, no successful content hash representing a valid statement or feed, no EventRevision, no EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO

http_status_policy.non_admitted_body_rule: a final non-200 body MUST NOT be used as parser input, and MUST NOT be hashed or persisted AS IF it were a successful admitted content body. Diagnostic transport provenance retained under existing raw primitives remains explicitly NON_ADMITTED.

not_modified.even_with_verified_prior_body: conditional caching and reuse remain unsupported even when a verified prior body exists. That prior body remains historical local data and is NOT substituted into this HTTP observation.
not_modified.rule: V1 does NOT reuse an old body in response to 304: no body hash, no new EventRevision, no reuse of a previous body, no synthesized body and no clean zero.
not_modified.why: deliberately avoids introducing a second cache/replay semantics into V1

partial_content.extends_fix8: this extends FIX8's "no incomplete prefix may be treated as a complete response" property to SERVER-DECLARED Partial Content. FIX8 covered truncation the CLIENT causes by aborting; 206 is incompleteness the SERVER declares, and arrives complete at the transport layer.
partial_content.rule: Range retrieval is unsupported in V1 and the client MUST NOT send Range or If-Range. A 206 received unexpectedly yields no successful body hash, no semantic parser input, no EventRevision and is never interpreted as a complete response.

http_status_policy.status_200_is_not_semantic_success: the status gate alone does NOT mean semantic success. An admitted body must still pass every existing gate: decoded-size bound, complete-body semantics, durable raw and hash, UTF-8, XML/HTML security, parser and classifier, and commit. 200 bypasses no existing validation.

http_policy.max_redirects_note: tightens urllib's default of 10; must be enforced explicitly

physical_attempt_deadline.address_policy: Resolved addresses are tried SEQUENTIALLY in resolver order, one TCP connection attempt at a time, each bounded by connect_timeout_seconds, all inside the same 60 s total deadline; the first established connection is used. No parallel or racing connection attempts (no Happy Eyeballs). All address attempts belong to ONE physical attempt and one unit. Resolution is one lookup with unspecified address family (IPv4 and IPv6), used in the order returned by the platform resolver.
physical_attempt_deadline.begins_at: PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START - the FIX15 grant-and-consume instant immediately before transport invocation
physical_attempt_deadline.boundary: An attempt succeeds at the network level only if its terminal network event occurs at monotonic elapsed e < 60 s from begins_at. At e = 60 s every unfinished attempt is expired.
physical_attempt_deadline.clock: MONOTONIC - the rate_limiter.clock domain of the current limiter epoch; wall-clock changes cannot shorten or extend it
covers: TCP connection establishment, including every resolved-address attempt
TLS handshake including certificate and hostname verification
content decoding required to produce admitted decoded body bytes
physical_attempt_deadline.ends_at: The network phase of an attempt ends when (a) the complete decoded body of a final exact-200 response is available, (b) the response is classified as an intermediate redirect or non-admitted final response, whose body is not drained (the connection is closed), or (c) the attempt fails.
physical_attempt_deadline.enforcement: At the total deadline the FOMC provider operation aborts the attempt logically. Observable requirements: a DNS result arriving after expiry is discarded; no TCP connection is initiated from it; no HTTP request byte is sent by the expired attempt; nothing received by it is admitted. Resolver activity inside the platform after logical cancellation (for example retransmissions of an abandoned lookup) is outside provider semantics unless the implementation chooses process isolation.

expiry.reobservation: obligation stays PENDING; further attempts follow revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.retry_policy
expiry.zero: blocked for the affected feed cycle or candidate

physical_attempt_deadline.post_network_stages: Durable persistence, hashing, text decoding, parsing, classification, normalization and commit are local stages outside this deadline and perform no network I/O.

redirects.logical_fetch_deadline: No additional logical-fetch deadline. Every attempt is individually bounded and at most 4 exist, so no active network attempt runs forever; limiter waits are finite while FIX15 grants.
redirects.rule: Each redirect-follow request is its own PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START with its own fresh 60-second deadline beginning at its own grant. Limiter waiting between attempts is counted against no attempt.

physical_attempt_deadline.slow_drip: A server sending one decoded byte every 29 s never trips the 30 s inactivity bound, but the attempt is aborted at elapsed 60 s. No complete body is admitted.

stage_limits.classification_invariance: Whichever limit fires, the outcome class is the same: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, no admission.
stage_limits.connect_timeout_seconds: http_policy.connect_timeout_seconds = 10, unchanged: bounds each TCP connection establishment attempt
stage_limits.dns: No separate DNS limit; DNS is bounded by the total deadline.
stage_limits.earliest_limit_wins: Every applicable limit is enforced; whichever expires first ends the attempt. Stage limits never extend the total deadline.
stage_limits.read_timeout_seconds: http_policy.read_timeout_seconds = 30, unchanged: an INACTIVITY bound on each individual blocking socket read or write, including TLS handshake I/O, status/header wait and each body read

proxy_policy.rule: provider requests ignore HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY and system proxy settings; no proxy auto-discovery; connections go directly to the validated host

raw_first_and_status.admitted_final_200: the durable raw body exists before any normalized semantic visibility - the existing raw-first guarantee is unchanged
raw_first_and_status.clarification: raw-first does NOT mean "parse every HTTP body regardless of status"
raw_first_and_status.diagnostic_digest_note: if a separate low-level diagnostic transport digest already exists by design, it must not be confused with the admitted content hash
raw_first_and_status.non_admitted_status: transport and status provenance may be durable under existing primitives, but there is NO admitted complete content body eligible for normal semantic replay or parsing

http_policy.read_timeout_note: matches the repo convention REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30; an inactivity bound whose coverage is frozen in http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline.stage_limits

redirect_implementation.automatic_redirect_following: FORBIDDEN - the HTTP client must never follow a redirect itself
redirect_implementation.connections: every physical attempt opens a new connection (its own DNS, TCP and TLS stages under its own deadline); no connection is reused across physical attempts
per_response: 1. read the status and headers of the response of the current physical attempt
2. if the status is an allowed redirect status: resolve Location under http_policy.redirect_policy (no URI-header fallback, no repair), validate the target completely BEFORE any network side effect
3. close the redirect response and its connection without draining its body; the redirect body is never semantic, never admitted and never read
4. obtain a separate FIX15 limiter grant for the next physical attempt, consuming one unit, with a fresh http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline
5. at most 3 followed redirects per logical fetch (http_policy.max_redirects); a 4th redirect is a redirect-limit failure
6. any other final status goes to http_policy.http_status_policy
redirect_implementation.timeouts: the transport must enforce connect_timeout_seconds and read_timeout_seconds separately, plus the total deadline

redirect_policy.allowed_statuses_rule: ONLY these intermediate redirect statuses may be FOLLOWED. A 3xx outside this set is a final non-admitted response: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
redirect_policy.body_rule: bodies attached to intermediate 301/302/303/307/308 responses are never semantic feed or statement bodies: no XML/HTML semantic parse and no EventRevision from a redirect body. Retained transport diagnostics remain non-admitted and must never influence the classifier.
redirect_policy.fourth_redirect_rule: the fourth redirect Location target MUST NOT be requested; the logical fetch terminates with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
redirect_policy.identity_rule: a final 200 reached through valid redirects may enter the normal pipeline, but identity remains the FIX4 authority: the official discovery link BEFORE redirects. The final URL stays non-identifying provenance and redirects NEVER re-key source_item_id.

algorithm.dot_segments: removed by the frozen reference-resolution algorithm. NO filesystem interpretation and NO local path normalization; the result is an HTTP URL passed to V1 security validation.

base.chain_rule: U0 requested -> Location L1 resolved against U0 -> request U1; U1 returns L2 resolved against U1 -> request U2. Later Locations are NEVER resolved against U0.
base.rule: the exact absolute request URL actually used for the CURRENT HTTP hop

fragment.must_not_hide_a_forbidden_component: removing the fragment must never conceal an otherwise forbidden query, host or scheme - every other URL check still applies to the resolved candidate
fragment.rule: resolution may produce a URI carrying a fragment; the already-frozen canonicalization then removes it from the actual HTTP request target. No second fragment policy is invented for redirects.

location_resolution.identity_rule: resolution derives only the next request_url for that transport hop. It NEVER changes canonical_primary_statement_url, source_item_id or the logical identity authority, which remains the official discovery link BEFORE redirects (FIX4) even across U0 -> U1 -> U2 relative chains.

location_value_preprocessing.trim_rule: remove ONLY surrounding HTTP optional whitespace (SP U+0020 and HTAB U+0009) from the beginning and end of the field value

order: 1. READ_LOCATION
2. TRIM_OUTER_HTTP_OWS (SP and HTAB only)
3. REJECT_EMPTY
4. PARSE_URI_REFERENCE
5. RESOLVE_AGAINST_CURRENT_REQUEST_URL
6. APPLY_EXISTING_V1_URL_SECURITY_AND_CANONICALIZATION
7. APPLY_EXISTING_FRAGMENT_NON_REQUEST_RULE
8. REQUEST_ONLY_IF_ADMITTED
location_resolution.order_rule: security validation MUST NOT be applied to the UNRESOLVED relative text as if it were already an absolute URL. Resolution precedes validation; validation is never weakened by it.

percent_escapes.rule: reference resolution MUST NOT percent-decode before FIX7 validation, and must apply no normalization that changes logical path semantics. Malformed forms such as %, %2 or %GG fail before any request.

location_resolution.redirect_body: UNCHANGED from FIX12 - non-semantic. Location derivation uses response METADATA only; a redirect body can never influence the target URL, the classifier, statement content or identity.
location_resolution.retries_untouched: FIX13 adds no retry rule; the existing frozen retry policy is unchanged.

security_after_resolution.no_special_redirect_security_regime: a resolved redirect target satisfies EXACTLY the same V1 constraints as any other URL. Being a redirect target grants no trust, and being absolute grants no special case.

supported_reference_forms.query_only_reference: syntactically resolvable, then subject to the unchanged V1 query policy

forbidden_heuristics: treating arbitrary text as a path
syntax.must_parse_as: exactly one URI-reference under the frozen resolution semantics

transition_accounting.rule: each successfully followed Location resolution consumes exactly ONE redirect transition from FIX12's maximum of 3. A REJECTED Location causes no target request and no transition follow; the response carrying it may still be recorded as transport provenance under existing semantics.

redirect_policy.location_rule: an allowed redirect status MUST carry a Location header. Its value is preprocessed, parsed as a URI-reference and RESOLVED against the current hop request URL per redirect_policy.location_resolution, and only the resolved absolute candidate is validated under the existing URL security and canonicalization rules. Missing Location, empty Location, a malformed reference or an unsafe resolved target all yield SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. The target is NEVER guessed or reconstructed.
redirect_policy.loop_rule: a loop such as A -> B -> A terminates via the redirect-transition limit at the latest. No hidden automatic redirect following beyond max_followed_transitions. An implementation may detect a loop sooner only if that alters no admitted content semantics; the frozen deterministic behaviour is the transition count.
redirect_policy.method_rule: FOMC V1 requests are GET only and every followed redirect remains a GET. No POST, no body-bearing redirect semantics, no library-dependent method choice.
redirect_policy.request_accounting: request_accounting applies independently before EVERY physical hop: a target admitted by FIX13 still must reacquire the shared provider limiter before any network side effect. HTTP auto-follow cannot bypass that gate.
redirect_policy.target_validation: before EACH redirect follow the target must pass all V1 redirect URL security checks - HTTPS, host allowlist, userinfo, port, percent syntax and the rest - and validation occurs BEFORE the network request, so an unsafe target is never contacted
redirect_policy.transition_semantics: max_redirects = 3 means AT MOST THREE FOLLOWED REDIRECT TRANSITIONS after the initial request. Initial request -> redirect #1 -> follow -> redirect #2 -> follow -> redirect #3 -> follow. If the response after following redirect #3 is itself another redirect, that is redirect #4.

http_policy.redirect_rule: validated BEFORE being followed; destination must stay on the allowlist; off-allowlist => fail closed, host never contacted
http_policy.user_agent_note: repo convention hyprl-trading-lab-<purpose>/<version>. No personal e-mail, no secret, no browser impersonation.

identity.aliasing_non_goal_v1: NO automatic alias equivalence or global deduplication across distinct normalized official discovery URLs is claimed. Different normalized identity URLs remain distinct logical source items unless an already-frozen conflict rule independently blocks admission. Do not merge using body hash, date, title, HTML canonical or final redirect destination; alias equivalence requires a separately frozen policy.
identity.canonical_primary_statement_url: normalize(official_discovery_link_before_redirect), where normalize is EXACTLY the existing url_canonicalization policy. The word canonical means the normalized official discovery-link URL selected by this identity policy; it does not mean the final response URL or a remote HTML canonical URL.
identity.canonical_url_boundary: FIX4 freezes WHICH INPUT enters existing URL normalization: the official discovery link BEFORE primary network redirects. URL normalization transforms and redirect security rules are unchanged. General alias resolution is not introduced. FIX3 date-correction stability remains intact.

conflict_policy.resolution: never 'latest wins'; persist diagnostics and raw provenance; identity.guid_policy_v2 is the deterministic resolution policy for GUID conflicts and admits events normally

date_correction.downstream_dedupe: D1 and corrected D2 are revision metadata of the SAME source_item_id; downstream MUST NOT count them as two independent logical FOMC events merely because the date changed
date_correction.existing_guid_conflicts: preserved unchanged; apply conflict_policy if independently triggered. A date correction by itself is NOT an identity conflict, and is never a reason to split the item.
date_correction.revision_metadata: official_statement_date belongs to the observed content revision. If H1/D1 becomes H2/D2 with a changed body hash, append a NEW immutable content revision under the SAME source_item_id. Retain H1/D1 intact; no overwrite. Identical-body discrepancies follow parser_policy.official_statement_date_determinism.
date_correction.rule: same provider_id + same event_family + same canonical_primary_statement_url => SAME logical source item, regardless of an official_statement_date correction
date_correction.visibility: each revision keeps source_available_at = null and source_updated_at = null; availability is carried per observation-to-revision link (observed_at and avail, revision_mode_neutrality). Identity repair never rewrites observed_at, ingested_at or declared_release_at. D2 is metadata, not source_updated_at, correction timing or content-vintage evidence; no retroactive availability change.
date_correction.with_guid: same canonical primary URL and same RSS GUID with D1 -> D2: SAME source_item_id; append a revision if the body hash changes
date_correction.without_guid: same canonical primary URL in historical archive/backfill with no RSS GUID and D1 -> D2: SAME source_item_id; append a revision if the body hash changes. GUID absence does not alter logical identity.

identity.discovery_link_mutation: a change in the official discovery link from U1 to a differently normalized U2 is NOT a redirect-topology change. The existing item keeps its stored U1-derived identity. A newly discovered U2 follows existing conflict/dedupe semantics only; no alias inference, identity rewrite or 'latest URL wins'.
identity.final_response_url_role: NON-IDENTIFYING TRANSPORT PROVENANCE: final allowlisted response URL after redirects. It MUST NOT replace canonical_primary_statement_url or re-key an item, including when it differs from discovery or changes on a later observation. Existing security validation still applies.
identity.guid_note: historical statements may lie outside current feed depth; identity must not depend on the feed

guid_policy_v2.baseline: the set of GUID values already recorded for the URL, and the set of URLs already recorded for the GUID, in the classification_order baseline
guid_policy_v2.identity_authority: the canonical discovery URL (identity.source_item_id); the RSS GUID is provenance only and never merges or splits items
guid_policy_v2.missing_guid: identity from the URL; the absence raises one GUID_MISSING diagnostic per item, never an identity failure and never blocking zero; no synthetic GUID; a first GUID on an item that had none starts its baseline without GUID_CONFLICT; a GUID that disappears raises nothing
guid_policy_v2.resolution_policy: GUID_CONFLICT and GUID_COLLISION make a cycle started by the raising record NOT_ZERO; GUID_MISSING never does; GUID diagnostics never withhold events, never merge or split items and are never item markers
guid_policy_v2.same_guid_different_urls: no merge: each URL is its own logical item processed independently; when the GUID's URL baseline is non-empty, a URL not in it raises one durable GUID_COLLISION diagnostic (recording the URL); the same URL never raises it again for that GUID
guid_policy_v2.same_url_different_guids: one logical item; when the URL's GUID baseline is non-empty, a GUID value not in it raises one durable GUID_CONFLICT diagnostic (recording the value); the same value never raises it again

identity.historical_discovery_url_role: the validated HISTORICAL_BACKFILL_MANIFEST_V1 entry (surfaces.backfill_manifest), persisted durably before any request, supplies the pre-redirect identity input under the same validation and normalization as LIVE. No synthesized URL from date; no RSS GUID required; no identity from final response or HTML canonical.
identity.html_canonical_role: NON-IDENTIFYING, NON-AUTHORITATIVE: <link rel="canonical"> is ignored for V1 semantics and logical identity. It MUST NOT replace canonical_primary_statement_url, change source_item_id, merge or split items, or override official discovery identity. A mismatch alone is NOT an identity conflict. If retained at all, it is optional diagnostic/provenance only; no network retrieval is authorized by this field.
identity.identity_url_input_stage: official statement link parsed from the already DURABLE official discovery artifact, BEFORE the primary HTTP request and BEFORE following any primary redirect
identity_url_order: 1. fetch and durably persist the official discovery artifact under existing raw-first/provenance rules
2. parse its official statement link U_discovered
3. validate U_discovered using existing V1 URL/security rules
4. apply the EXISTING frozen url_canonicalization policy to U_discovered
5. bind the resulting value as canonical_primary_statement_url
6. compute source_item_id from provider_id, event_family and that value using existing canonical_serialization
7. perform the primary HTTP request for the discovered statement under existing HTTP policy
9. persist the redirect chain and U_final as transport provenance under existing raw policy
identity.identity_url_precomputation: computing a candidate identity before the primary fetch does NOT admit an EventRevision or an IN_SCOPE_V1 event; existing primary classification, raw-first, normalization and server-attested visibility (causal_predicates.avail) requirements remain mandatory
identity.live_discovery_url_role: the official monetary-policy RSS item's <link> extracted from its durable feed artifact supplies the pre-redirect identity input. Validate it, apply existing normalization and derive source_item_id before primary redirects. RSS GUID remains discovery provenance/consistency signal only.
identity.missing_canonical_url: FAIL CLOSED under the existing identity policy if a stable canonical primary URL cannot be established. No date fallback, no (provider_id, event_family, date) fallback and no GUID+date fallback may manufacture a logical identity.

provenance_url_roles.discovered_url: official statement link extracted from the durable discovery artifact; only its existing-policy normalized value supplies the logical URL identity
provenance_url_roles.final_response_url: final allowlisted URL after primary redirects, corresponding to existing raw policy's final URL provenance
provenance_url_roles.redirect_chain: ordered transport provenance of the primary request hops
provenance_url_roles.request_url: URL actually requested at a given hop; transport provenance, not a replacement identity input after derivation
provenance_url_roles.storage_note: semantic roles within existing raw/observation provenance, not a new raw or normalized schema; keep discovery provenance distinct from request, redirect and final response provenance

identity.redirect_identity_role: NON-IDENTIFYING TRANSPORT PROVENANCE: redirect destinations and the ordered redirect chain MUST NOT replace the discovered identity URL, merge or split items, or re-key source_item_id. Redirect differences alone are NOT identity conflicts; existing independent GUID conflicts remain unchanged.
identity.redirect_topology_change_behavior: for the same provider_id, event_family and normalized official discovery URL, U1 -> U2 then U1 -> U3 yields the SAME canonical_primary_statement_url = normalize(U1) and the SAME source_item_id. Transport movement alone creates neither a logical item nor a content revision: identical body follows same_item_same_body_hash; changed body follows same_item_different_body_hash under that same item.
identity.reobservation_identity_stability: scheduled re-observations retain the stored canonical_primary_statement_url derived from original discovery U1. A request may start from that official identity URL; the final destination observed that day MUST NOT recompute or rewrite item identity. No scheduler, recheck-anchor or deadline semantics change.
identity.revision_id: revision_policy.revision_mode_neutrality: an EventRevision is keyed by (source item, content hash); the design rev4 derivation from (observation, content_hash, gating timestamps) is overridden (binds.design_overrides)
identity.rss_guid_role: OFFICIAL DISCOVERY IDENTIFIER AND PROVENANCE ONLY - not business identity, not revision identity, not proof of unchanged content
identity.source_item_id: SHA-256 using canonical_serialization over the ordered JSON array [provider_id, event_family, canonical_primary_statement_url], containing exactly those three string values in that order. No other field participates in the logical item hash or identity dedupe.
identity.source_observation_id: design rev4: derived from (provider, source_item_id, content_hash); NEVER URL alone
identity.uniqueness_claim: NOT contractually documented by the provider; identity quality remains GOOD, not EXCELLENT

invariants.F01: Only official allowlisted Federal Reserve surfaces may contribute.
invariants.F02: RSS is discovery, never source-time authority.
invariants.F03: The primary statement page is the semantic authority.
invariants.F04: declared_release_at requires a strict explicit date PLUS an explicit EST/EDT release grammar; it is NEVER a content visibility gate.
invariants.F06: observed_at is the real primary-statement acquisition instant.
invariants.F08: Raw is made durable before any parse.
invariants.F09: Same logical item with changed bytes appends a new immutable revision. For the same provider_id, event_family and canonical_primary_statement_url, mutable content metadata corrections, including official_statement_date, MUST preserve source_item_id; the prior revision remains intact.
invariants.F10: Same bytes create no duplicate revision.
invariants.F11: Last Update never advances original source availability.
invariants.F12: The provider numeric rate limit remains UNKNOWN; the client ceiling is HyprL policy only.
invariants.F13: Raw redistribution is disabled in V1.
invariants.F14: Unknown upstream correction semantics never imply immutability.
invariants.F16: No market, outcome, consensus or LLM field exists in the capture layer.
invariants.F17: The CaptureSpec hash is bound into every normalized revision.
invariants.F18: Unsupported release syntax never guesses a time: declared_release_at is null with RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED, and the EventRevision is not withheld on that ground.
invariants.F19: RELEASE TIME IS NOT CONTENT-VINTAGE PROOF. A provider-declared logical release timestamp must never be used as the source availability of a captured content revision unless the provider contract proves that exact revision became available at that timestamp. For FOMC V1 no such revision-specific proof exists.
invariants.F20: BACKFILL CONTENT VINTAGE. Historical backfill content is visible only from its actual observed/durable timeline unless exact vintage provenance exists. An original release timestamp may describe event metadata but cannot retroactively date the fetched body.
invariants.F21: REVISION-SPECIFIC AVAILABILITY. A later observed content revision cannot inherit an earlier logical event release timestamp as its own source availability. Each revision requires its own availability evidence; absent provider evidence, source_available_at = null.
invariants.F22: ABSENCE CLAIM CANNOT EXCEED CLASSIFIER COVERAGE. An absence assertion must never cover a semantic family broader than the frozen classifier's proven coverage. Where classifier completeness is not established, zero is scoped to the capture predicate only.
invariants.F23: AN ITEM MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ZERO ONLY IF IT IS ITEM_SEMANTICALLY_CONCLUDED (zero_assertion.outstanding_relevant_item.concluded). Every other item blocks EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO in every cycle, listed or not. Backfill records never count.
invariants.F24: DISCOVERY/PRIMARY CLASSIFICATION CONFLICT FAILS CLOSED. CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT is never ITEM_SEMANTICALLY_CONCLUDED: no event, no zero, no silent downgrade; a later LIVE_ELIGIBLE normalized or DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE outcome, or a valid RESOLVE, concludes it.
invariants.F25: MUTABLE CONTENT METADATA MUST NOT DEFINE LOGICAL IDENTITY. Mutable statement metadata parsed from primary-page content, including official_statement_date, MUST NOT participate in source_item_id, the logical item hash or identity dedupe. With provider_id and event_family fixed and the same frozen canonical_primary_statement_url, date corrections preserve the logical item, with or without RSS GUID. Changed bytes append revisions; identical verified bytes under the same CaptureSpec hash must yield the same date, otherwise FAIL CLOSED with no new content revision and no overwrite.
invariants.F26: DISCOVERY URL ANCHORS LOGICAL IDENTITY. For FOMC V1, canonical_primary_statement_url is the official statement link parsed from durable official discovery provenance BEFORE primary redirects, validated and normalized under existing V1 rules. Redirect destinations, final response URLs and HTML canonical URLs are non-identifying provenance and MUST NOT replace this identity input. The rule applies to LIVE feed and HISTORICAL_BACKFILL manifest discovery (surfaces.backfill_manifest), with or without RSS GUID. The admitted HTTPS scheme MUST be serialized as exactly lowercase ASCII https in the identity URL; original scheme spelling MUST NOT be hashed as the scheme component of canonical_primary_statement_url. Apply the existing hostname normalization unchanged and serialize the canonical authority WITHOUT any port component: an absent port and admitted explicit decimal 443 MUST yield the exact same identity URL. Original explicit default-port spelling MUST NOT be hashed as a port component of canonical_primary_statement_url. Any malformed percent escape makes the discovery URL inadmissible: no canonical_primary_statement_url or source_item_id may be derived/admitted from it. Validate percent syntax before normalization/identity and before any request; no repair or percent-decoding is introduced by this gate.
invariants.F27: TRANSPORT REDIRECTION MUST NOT REKEY AN ITEM. With provider_id, event_family and the normalized official discovery URL fixed, U1 -> U2 and later U1 -> U3 MUST produce the same source_item_id from normalize(U1). Transport movement alone cannot split logical history, cause an identity conflict or create a content revision; changed bytes append revisions under the same item, and unchanged bytes do not duplicate revisions.
invariants.F28: HTTPS SCHEME CASE CANNOT ALTER LOGICAL IDENTITY. HTTPS scheme admission is ASCII case-insensitive; the canonical identity scheme is always exactly lowercase ASCII https. With provider_id, event_family and every other URL component unchanged, changing only upstream HTTPS scheme case MUST preserve canonical_primary_statement_url and source_item_id and MUST NOT create an identity conflict or content revision. Non-HTTPS and empty/missing schemes are rejected, never silently upgraded. Original source spelling is raw discovery provenance only.
invariants.F29: EXPLICIT DEFAULT HTTPS PORT CANNOT ALTER LOGICAL IDENTITY. For otherwise identical admitted official discovery URLs, with provider_id and event_family fixed, an absent port and explicit decimal port 443 MUST produce byte-identical canonical_primary_statement_url values WITHOUT a port component and the SAME source_item_id. Default-port spelling alone MUST NOT create a logical item, identity conflict or content revision. Any other explicit port or malformed port is rejected before source_item_id derivation and before any request; never silently stripped, rewritten or interpreted as absent/default. Raw explicit-port spelling remains provenance only.
invariants.F30: MALFORMED PERCENT ESCAPES ARE REJECTED BEFORE IDENTITY OR REQUEST. Every literal % in an admitted V1 URL must begin PCT_ENCODED = % HEXDIG HEXDIG, with exactly two ASCII hex digits from 0-9, A-F or a-f. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED before canonical identity/source_item_id derivation or admission, before a primary request, and before redirect follow. This mandatory syntax gate does not decode, re-encode, repair or provide a literal-percent fallback. Valid escapes remain subject to existing component restrictions and path-preservation semantics; no new equivalence or hex-case normalization is introduced. Durable raw source text is not mutated.
invariants.F31: DECODED BODY SIZE IS ENFORCED DURING PRODUCTION. For every body consumed under V1's existing decoded-size policy, count decoded entity-body bytes incrementally from zero before charset/text decoding. Enforce the feed 2097152-byte or statement 5242880-byte cap during bounded output production, not after unbounded decompression. If the next output would exceed the cap, stop body decoding immediately, do not append excess bytes and do not continue to learn final size. Exactly the cap passes the size gate; cap + 1 rejects. Content-Length or compressed size cannot replace this gate. No oversized body or incomplete prefix reaches text decoding, XML/HTML parsing or normalization, becomes a complete admitted raw artifact or successful complete-body hash, or produces an EventRevision. Reuse PARSER_FAILED, never EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO. Existing successful-body hash/persistence/replay bytes and raw-first order remain unchanged.
invariants.F32: TEXT DECODING IS SINGLE-VALUED AND STRICT UTF-8. Both V1 XML and HTML bodies use only UTF-8, also the explicit default when signals are absent. Every recognized HTTP/BOM/document encoding signal must be UTF-8-compatible under text_decoding_v1, or cause PARSER_FAILED; labels are limited to utf-8 and utf8 after the frozen ASCII-only label normalization. No competing authority, heuristic detection, fallback decoder, lossy error handling or platform codec/alias selection. Invalid UTF-8 and unsupported BOMs fail closed. Exactly one leading UTF-8 BOM is an encoding signature omitted from semantic text, never removed from raw/hash/replay bytes. Same verified admitted bytes plus persisted relevant HTTP metadata plus the same CaptureSpec hash MUST produce the same Unicode text or PARSER_FAILED. Charset failure preserves raw provenance, creates no EventRevision and cannot establish zero for an affected feed/candidate. Existing Unicode/whitespace transformations and FIX1-FIX8 remain unchanged.
invariants.F33: HTML SEMANTIC ANCHORS ARE UNIQUE AND AUTHORITATIVE. primary_page_title is the unique h3.title within the frozen article-heading region; official_statement_date the unique p.article__time; release_line the unique p.releaseTime start element.
