No document-metadata, inline-SVG, global-text or traversal-order fallback may substitute. Zero or more than one title or date match: PARSER_FAILED; zero or more than one release-line match: non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED.
invariants.F34: RELEASE LINE EXTENT IS TOKEN-BOUND, NOT RECOVERED-DOM-BOUND. release_line consists only of the leading character-data segment following the unique p.releaseTime start tag and preceding the next markup token. Recovered descendant .textContent is forbidden as authority. This closes the observed unclosed-paragraph problem.
invariants.F35: SEMANTIC TEXT NORMALIZATION ORDER IS SINGLE-VALUED: (1) character-reference-aware field extraction, (2) NFC, (3) ASCII-whitespace collapse, (4) U+0020 trim, (5) exact compare or strict parse. No reordering.
invariants.F36: XML DISCOVERY PARSING HAS NO DTD / CUSTOM-ENTITY / XINCLUDE EXPANSION PATH. FOMC V1 discovery XML forbids DOCTYPE and XInclude. External DTDs, external general entities and external parameter entities are never resolved. Custom internal entity declarations are unsupported because DOCTYPE is forbidden, so the billion-laughs family is rejected before expansion. Parsing performs no network or filesystem resolution. Security rejection is PARSER_FAILED and blocks EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO.
invariants.F37: HTTP BODY SIZE BOUNDS AND XML EXPANSION SECURITY ARE DISTINCT. The FIX8 feed cap of 2097152 bytes applies to decoded HTTP input bytes. XML parser safety does NOT rely on that cap to bound entity or XInclude expansion; parser-level amplification mechanisms are forbidden outright by FIX11.
invariants.F38: ONLY FINAL HTTP 200 CAN PRODUCE AN ADMITTED CONTENT BODY. Only exact final status 200 may enter the normal body, hash, text-decoding, parser and revision pipeline. Any other final status is non-admitted and cannot produce an EventRevision or a clean zero. Body appearance never overrides status.
invariants.F39: PARTIAL / EMPTY / NOT-MODIFIED RESPONSES CANNOT MASQUERADE AS COMPLETE CONTENT. 206, 204 and 304 are unsupported and non-admitted in V1. No prior-body reuse on 304, no Range requests, no conditional requests, and no successful complete-body hash or revision from any of these statuses.
invariants.F40: REDIRECT FOLLOWING IS EXPLICITLY BOUNDED AND NON-IDENTIFYING. Only 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308 may be followed, at most 3 transitions, with every target security-validated before the request. The fourth redirect target is never requested. Redirect bodies are non-semantic and identity remains the pre-redirect official discovery URL.
invariants.F41: CACHE VALIDATORS ARE PROVENANCE, NEVER CONTENT-VINTAGE PROOF. ETag, Last-Modified and HTTP caching metadata cannot populate or infer causal content-availability timestamps. Conditional requests are disabled in V1.
invariants.F42: REDIRECT LOCATION IS RESOLVED AGAINST THE CURRENT REQUEST URL BEFORE SECURITY VALIDATION. Location is an HTTP URI-reference; relative and scheme-relative references are supported. The base is the actual absolute request URL of the CURRENT redirect hop and advances with each hop. Resolution occurs before target security validation, and the resolved absolute target must then satisfy all existing V1 URL admission rules. No browser repair, no identity effect.
invariants.F43: REDIRECT REFERENCE RESOLUTION CANNOT WEAKEN URL SECURITY. Relative resolution may never bypass HTTPS-only, the host allowlist, the userinfo prohibition, port rules, the query prohibition, percent-escape validation or the fragment non-request semantics. An unsafe resolved target is never contacted.
invariants.F44: PROVIDER RATE ACCOUNTING COUNTS PHYSICAL ATTEMPT STARTS, NOT LOGICAL FETCHES. Each independently attempted HTTP request under the FOMC V1 provider consumes exactly one PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START unit when permission to begin is granted, BEFORE network side effects, with no refund on failure. Feed, primary, every followed redirect, permitted later reattempt, scheduled recheck and historical provider GET all count. A logical fetch with three redirect follows consumes four units; rejected or unfollowed targets create no additional attempt or unit.
invariants.F45: ALL FOMC V1 NETWORK CATEGORIES SHARE ONE PROVIDER ACCOUNTING DOMAIN. Every physical attempt passes through the same FEDERAL_RESERVE_PROVIDER_V1_GLOBAL accounting/limiter gate. Independent feed, primary, recheck, redirect and historical quota buckets are forbidden; redirect/retry internals and category-specific queues cannot bypass aggregate provider admission. No logical fetch reserves a multi-request corridor.
invariants.F46: PROVIDER RATE CEILING USES A ROLLING 60-SECOND PHYSICAL-START WINDOW. For candidate monotonic t, include prior admitted s iff 0 < t - s < 60; admission requires at most five such prior starts. For every admitted t, (t-60s,t] contains at most six PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START events. At t=60 after starts 0,10,20,30,40,50, start 0 is excluded and candidate 60 is admitted if spacing and epoch preconditions pass. No fixed-minute, token-bucket or leaky-bucket substitute.
invariants.F47: MINIMUM SPACING IS PROVIDER-WIDE START-TO-START. A candidate requires t - previous_start >= 10 seconds; exact equality passes. Accounting, window and spacing use the SAME PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START atomic grant-and-consume event immediately before transport invocation. Completion time cannot shift the reference. No category or redirect/recheck exemption, no stored or reusable permit and no refund after grant, including cancellation before network I/O.
invariants.F48: RATE ADMISSION IS ATOMIC AND MONOTONIC WITHIN A LIMITER EPOCH. All concurrent candidates, across every FOMC V1 category/process emitter, pass through one provider-wide atomic inspect/test/grant/register decision over comparable monotonic history before transport. Stale-state double grants and simultaneous starts are forbidden; later candidates see prior grants. UTC/NTP/manual/timezone/DST changes cannot alter elapsed admission. The coordination primitive is unspecified.
invariants.F49: NEW LIMITER EPOCHS FAIL CONSERVATIVELY CLOSED FOR 60 SECONDS. Every fresh limiter epoch requires exclusive provider ownership and no attempt for its first 60 monotonic seconds; exact elapsed 60 passes the embargo. The epoch embargo begins only once old independent issuers can no longer initiate attempts. Independent overlapping epochs cannot both emit. After embargo, admission uses fresh current-epoch history; precise prior-epoch monotonic history is not reused and durable per-request history is not required. UTC history cannot shorten the embargo.
invariants.F50: REOBSERVATION GRID IS ANCHORED TO THE FIRST LIVE_ELIGIBLE PRIMARY OBSERVATION'S observed_at. For each logical FOMC source item, the anchor is exactly observed_at of its LIVE_ELIGIBLE (causal_predicates) primary record with the smallest commit_seq; LIVE_ELIGIBLE is fixed at commit, so the anchor never moves. Request/header time, raw durability commit, normalization, revision creation and later observations never define it. Obligations are A+300, A+3600, A+86400 and A+604800.
invariants.F51: DURABILITY DETERMINES ANCHOR SURVIVAL, NOT ANCHOR TIME. A volatile observation lost before the required raw/SourceObservation durability boundary creates no reconstructible anchor. Once the qualifying observation is durable, its original observed_at remains the anchor across crashes and restarts, even before normalized commit and after downstream parser/normalization failure. No restart-relative or commit-relative re-anchoring, no inferred anchor from lost volatile state, and no later revision or limiter delay may shift the grid.
invariants.F52: DURABLE REOBSERVATION ANCHOR IMPLIES FOUR REQUIRED LOGICAL OBLIGATIONS. At the existing qualifying original anchor durability boundary, exactly four logical obligations exist for offsets 300,3600,86400,604800 and targets original observed_at plus offset. No scheduler-specific write or normalized EventRevision commit is required for logical existence. Missing or partial materialization and crash after anchor durability cannot erase them; without a qualifying durable anchor no set can be derived from a lost volatile observation. This freezes membership, not execution or completion.
invariants.F53: REOBSERVATION OBLIGATION IDENTITY IS DERIVED AND IDEMPOTENT. The authoritative logical key is (source_item_id, original_reobservation_anchor_observed_at, offset_seconds), using exclusively the original FIX16 anchor and one of the four fixed offsets. Repeated/concurrent recovery, materialization, lost materialization ACK, same-body reobservation, parser recovery and H1 -> H2 cannot add logical checkpoints or a second grid. Duplicate rows denote the same member; different source items with equal anchor times remain distinct. Physical encoding and status/completion semantics are not prescribed.
invariants.F54: PAST-DUE OBLIGATIONS REMAIN REQUIRED. A PENDING reobservation obligation stays required after due_at, with no MISSED, EXPIRED, FAILED or other terminal state from lateness or failure (a SUSPENDED retry episode is a work-item state, not an obligation status). After downtime it becomes eligible subject to selection and FIX15, and is satisfied only by a real later observation with its own observed_at; no backdating, synthesis or due_at rewrite, and late execution never shifts any target.
invariants.F55: ONE DURABLE REOBSERVATION MAY SATISFY ALL DUE OBLIGATIONS FOR ITS ITEM. A qualifying observation R of S satisfies exactly the obligations of S with due_at <= R.observed_at, never those with a later due_at and never another item's. Several overdue obligations produce one logical fetch, not catch-up GETs, and satisfaction claims no earlier source state.
invariants.F56: OBLIGATION SATISFACTION OCCURS AT THE DURABLE SOURCE OBSERVATION BOUNDARY. Satisfaction requires a LIVE_ELIGIBLE per-response record (causal_predicates) of an admitted final exact-200 complete primary response. Changed content, parse success, a new EventRevision and normalized commit are not required; a durable LIVE_ELIGIBLE observation followed by parser failure satisfies the obligation while health records PARSER_FAILED.
invariants.F57: FAILED ATTEMPTS DO NOT SATISFY OR ERASE OBLIGATIONS. Transport, deadline, redirect, non-200, incomplete, content-coding, oversize, persistence-loss, clock-anomaly and cancellation outcomes leave the obligation PENDING. Further provider work follows BOUNDED_RETRY_EPISODE_V2: at most 6 attempts per durable episode key (backoff 60/300/900/3600/14400 s), then SUSPENDED; no tight loop, no hidden retry.
invariants.F58: SATISFACTION IS CRASH- AND ACK-RECONSTRUCTIBLE. Obligation status is derived only from the durable anchor and durable qualifying observation records. Completion rows are caches; losing a marker or an ACK never causes a provider request, and a volatile observation lost before durability satisfies nothing.
invariants.F59: FEED, REOBSERVATION AND BACKFILL WORK CANNOT STARVE EACH OTHER. All work shares the FIX15 limiter. Class rotation derives from durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED records; within classes (next eligible instant, source_item_id) ordering and final bounded episodes guarantee service. Queue pressure, restart or later feed contents never delete required work.
invariants.F60: EVERY PHYSICAL NETWORK ATTEMPT HAS A 60-SECOND ACTIVITY-INDEPENDENT TOTAL DEADLINE. It starts at PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START after limiter waiting, is monotonic, never resets on received bytes, and covers DNS, TCP, TLS, request write, headers, body and content decoding. Connect 10 s and read-inactivity 30 s still apply and the earliest limit wins. Each redirect-follow attempt has its own deadline. Expiry aborts logically: a late DNS result is discarded, no TCP connection or HTTP byte follows, nothing is admitted, and it maps to SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
invariants.F61: ZERO IS CYCLE-LOCAL AND SEES OUTSTANDING WORK. EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO holds for one LIVE cycle iff its LIVE_ELIGIBLE feed record parses, every earlier PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record is FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL (classified in commit_seq order, or terminally failed) before B, its own classification introduces no new, unidentifiable or first-sighted unsupported item and raises no GUID or feed-title diagnostic, and the pre-cycle state (commit_seq < B) holds no OUTSTANDING item. Every PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record is classified, eligible or not. The conclusion is durable and never rewritten; backfill never blocks it.
invariants.F62: EST/EDT ARE LITERAL FIXED-OFFSET SOURCE LABELS AND RELEASE-CLOCK PARSING IS NON-GATING. EST = UTC-05:00 and EDT = UTC-04:00 regardless of season, with no timezone database. Any other, missing or malformed release clock gives declared_release_at = null and RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED; no zone is guessed and the EventRevision is not withheld.
invariants.F63: RELEVANCE NEEDS EVIDENCE BOTH WAYS. Every new safe feed item in the monetary family is acquired; DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE requires a successfully parsed primary page with both titles non-matching (a healthy negative, not PARSER_FAILED). URL shape is never negative evidence: unforeseen safe paths are UNRESOLVED and outstanding.
invariants.F64: SNAPSHOTS FOLLOW THE LATEST DURABLE RECORD WITHIN P(T). events_as_of and InformationSnapshot use FOMC_CURRENT_CONTENT_SELECTION_V1 and read every input only within the commit_seq prefix P(T): content is current only when the latest PROCESSABLE record, or the latest verified record of the same hash, maps to a revision; a corrupt or unverified newest record gives a barrier. An older revision is never current and source activity is never absence.
invariants.F65: AUTONOMOUS PROVIDER TRAFFIC IS ABSOLUTELY BOUNDED. Retry episodes are durable, keyed without wall time, opened once per key and closed only by final EPISODE_SUCCEEDED/EPISODE_SUSPENDED records; attempts are counted by durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED records, committed before any network I/O and never uncounted. A LIVE item has at most 5 autonomous keys, so at most 5 x 6 x 4 = 120 physical requests, whatever restarts, clock steps, relisting or recovery occur, under retry_policy.upper_bound_proof.store_assumption.
invariants.F66: LOCAL FAILURE NEVER CAUSES EXTRA PROVIDER TRAFFIC. Commit and corruption failures cause none; a durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED always counts as one attempt of its bounded episode, whatever happens after it; without a committed TRANSPORT_INVOKED no request can start.
invariants.F67: REDIRECTS ARE FOLLOWED ONLY BY A MANUAL LOOP. Automatic client redirect following is non-conforming; each hop is validated before contact, takes its own limiter grant and deadline, and at most 3 are followed. No existing repo opener is claimed to conform.
invariants.F68: HISTORICAL BACKFILL IS A FROZEN MANIFEST WITHOUT A RECHECK GRID. The manifest byte format is fixed, validated whole before any request (<= 1000 raw entries), persisted with hash and canonical work list; backfill never creates anchors or obligations, never blocks LIVE zero and never pre-empts LIVE and never satisfies LIVE obligations.
invariants.F69: DURABLE ACQUISITION WORK SURVIVES FEED DISAPPEARANCE. A LIVE acquisition created by any feed record's classification stays required until concluded or suspended, whatever later feeds list.
invariants.F70: DURABLE ORDER IS commit_seq; AVAILABILITY IS SERVER-ATTESTED. Every transaction commits. Its availability is the observed_at + 92 s of the first (by commit_seq) verified response, other than LATE_EVIDENCE, whose request began after it (never earlier than its own observed_at or earlier availability), unresolved until then. No local reading other than a verified observed_at enters availability; nothing is reordered or re-stamped.
invariants.F71: CAUSAL EFFECTS NEED LIVE_ELIGIBLE; PROCESSING NEEDS ONLY PROCESSABLE. Every PROCESSABLE record is processed regardless of clock evidence. Only a LIVE_ELIGIBLE record (PROCESSABLE, LIVE, verified by its own server Date/Age) anchors, starts a cycle, satisfies, succeeds, concludes or proves LIVE availability. Under causal_predicates.assumption, clock faults never stall capture and never create early visibility.
invariants.F72: RAW CORRUPTION FAILS CLOSED EVERYWHERE. A digest mismatch found in processing, recovery, reconciliation or replay prevents parsing, yields CORRUPTION_FAIL_CLOSED, marks dependent revisions NORMALIZED_PRESENT_RAW_CORRUPT and never triggers a refetch.
invariants.F73: OPERATOR RESOLUTIONS HAVE A COMMIT_SEQ CUTOFF. A RESOLVE is valid only when every per-response item record is RECORD_PROCESSING_TERMINAL and no LIVE episode or MANUAL_RETRY episode of LIVE work of the item is open; it covers exactly the records up to its own commit_seq; any later item record re-opens the item; there is no content-based exemption.
invariants.F74: EVENT REVISIONS ARE MODE-NEUTRAL; AVAILABILITY IS OBSERVATION-SPECIFIC. A revision is keyed by content hash; each qualifying IN_SCOPE observation links to it with its own mode and availability; LIVE availability requires a LIVE link; backfill never taints or pre-empts LIVE.
invariants.F75: LOCAL PROCESSING WORK DERIVES FROM DURABLE RECORDS AND HAS ONE OWNER. The epoch owner, driven by a periodic tick, runs at most one fenced run per record with a 600 s deadline; dead runs count toward the poison guard; derivable scheduler records are re-derived until committed; local failures never cause provider traffic.
invariants.F76: HTTP CLOCK HEADERS ARE PARSED STRICTLY. Only the final 200 response's single Date (strict IMF-fixdate, no leap second) and at most one Age (0..2147483647; <= 86400 for the clock check) are clock evidence; duplicates or invalid values make the reference unusable.
invariants.F77: RSS GUID IS PROVENANCE, URL IS IDENTITY. Same URL with a new GUID is one item plus GUID_CONFLICT; one GUID on a new URL never merges, plus GUID_COLLISION; a missing GUID is a diagnostic only; GUID values are never markers.
invariants.F78: AN ATTEMPT HAS ONE OUTCOME; LATE RESPONSES ARE FAIL-SAFE EVIDENCE. Every logical fetch has at most one outcome, the first committed; a per-response record is its attempt's outcome only while the attempt has none. A later response is kept and processed as unverified LATE_EVIDENCE: it can add candidates, markers and diagnostics or reopen an item, never conclude, anchor, satisfy, start a cycle or become current content.
invariants.F79: ZERO IS EXPOSED ONLY FOR THE NEWEST FEED RECORD. A snapshot shows EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO only when it is the conclusion of the latest processable LIVE feed record in P(T); otherwise NO_CURRENT_CYCLE or DISCOVERY_PENDING. An older zero is never presented as current.

item_predicate.backfill_discovery_side: a HISTORICAL_BACKFILL_MANIFEST_V1 entry replaces the feed-title conjunct for backfill observations (primary_classification_v2.inputs)

classification_states.DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE: outside the V1 subset on positive evidence: a successfully extracted primary title and the feed title both differ from the exact strings (primary_classification_v2). It may still be an FOMC-related publication (for example minutes); V1 does not capture it.
classification_states.IN_SCOPE_V1: both the recorded feed title (or manifest entry) and the primary title equal the frozen exact strings and the date anchor succeeds
classification_states.UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE: neither in nor definitely out of the V1 subset: classification conflict, unsupported discovery shape, or no successful classification yet

item_predicate.default_non_match: DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE only through primary_classification_v2 on a successfully extracted title; every other non-match is UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE
item_predicate.default_rationale: A negative requires positive evidence: a successfully parsed primary page whose title, and the feed title, both fail the exact V1 predicate. URL structure is never negative evidence. Anything that cannot be concluded that way stays UNRESOLVED and outstanding.
item_predicate.evidence: title verified on the four FOMC statement feed items and on statement pages sampled 2015-2026

feed_item_classification_v2.FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL: a PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record whose classification, or any terminal processing outcome (channel-level PARSER_FAILED, INTERNAL_PROCESSING_ERROR, CORRUPTION_FAIL_CLOSED), has committed
feed_item_classification_v2.applies_to: every PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record, whether or not it is LIVE_ELIGIBLE: its classification is its processing outcome (committed with its candidates, unidentifiable-item records, acquisitions and diagnostics) and has no causal effect; for a LIVE_ELIGIBLE feed record the cycle conclusion commits in the same transaction
feed_item_classification_v2.backfill_independence: HISTORICAL_BACKFILL records never make a LIVE feed item KNOWN; an item seen only through backfill is a NEW_FEED_CANDIDATE when LIVE first lists it
feed_item_classification_v2.classification_order: PROCESSABLE LIVE feed records (LATE_EVIDENCE included) are classified strictly in commit_seq order: a record is classified only after every earlier PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record is FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL. Its baseline is the durable state before its own commit_seq plus every earlier feed record's classification (candidates, titles, GUIDs, diagnostics). A run's 600 s deadline starts only once every earlier feed record is FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL, so waiting never counts toward DEAD. The result is a pure function of commit_seq order, identical in replay.
feed_item_classification_v2.creation_boundary: steps are evaluated against the baseline of classification_order; candidate and acquisition creation is idempotent per source_item_id and enforced by unique keys at commit
feed_item_classification_v2.feed_title_change: the baseline is the set of normalized feed titles already recorded for the item in the classification_order baseline (the birth title and every title raised by earlier diagnostics). A listed title not in that set raises one durable FEED_TITLE_CHANGED diagnostic (recording the new value) with the record's classification, making a cycle started by that record NOT_ZERO; the same value never raises it again. A new value equal to feed_title_exact is a marker (outstanding_relevant_item.concluded). Classification of observations keeps using the birth title; no traffic is created.
feed_item_classification_v2.invalid_title: an item with an admitted link but a missing, duplicated, invalid or child-element title is a normal candidate (acquired as usual) with an INVALID_FEED_TITLE marker; its recorded birth title is null (never equal to feed_title_exact)
feed_item_classification_v2.missing_title_on_known_item: a missing, duplicated or invalid title on an item that already has a candidate record raises nothing and leaves its title baseline unchanged
feed_item_classification_v2.no_structural_negative: no path or suffix shape is ever evidence that an item is irrelevant; 'a' and 'b' suffixes are treated identically; an unforeseen safe official path is UNRESOLVED (step 2), never DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE
feed_item_classification_v2.same_item_in_record: several items of one feed record that resolve to the same source_item_id are one item. For a new item the lexicographically smallest valid normalized title is the birth title (null if none is valid, with INVALID_FEED_TITLE); for any item whose GUID baseline is empty the smallest GUID starts it; every other value then follows feed_title_change and identity.guid_policy_v2 as if listed after it. The birth title therefore comes from the earliest classified feed record (by commit_seq) that lists the item.
steps: 1. an item whose link element is missing, duplicated, invalid or contains a child element, or whose link fails URL admission or identity derivation -> UNIDENTIFIABLE_ITEM: a durable item-level record keyed by SHA-256 of canonical_serialization of [raw link text or null, raw title text or null, raw guid text or null] is created on first sighting of that key (a cycle started by that record is NOT_ZERO); the rest of the feed is processed normally

2. link admitted (https, www.federalreserve.gov, port 443, valid URL) but the canonical path does not match surfaces.statement_family_path -> UNSUPPORTED_DISCOVERY_SHAPE: on first sighting a durable LIVE feed candidate record (recording the normalized feed title and GUID provenance) with outcome UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE is created and a cycle started by that record is NOT_ZERO; no primary GET; outstanding until an operator resolution, after which later listings are non-blocking

3. family path and a LIVE feed candidate record exists in the classification_order baseline -> existing item: KNOWN if it is not an OUTSTANDING_RELEVANT_ITEM, otherwise OUTSTANDING (no new acquisition; the durable acquisition is reused)

4. family path and no LIVE feed candidate record exists -> NEW_FEED_CANDIDATE: a durable LIVE feed candidate record (recording the normalized feed title and GUID provenance) and one LIVE_ACQUISITION are created with the record's classification; a cycle started by that record is NOT_ZERO
feed_item_classification_v2.within_record_order: items of one feed record are classified in document order; each sees the candidate, GUID and URL records produced by earlier items of the same record (so two URLs picking up one new GUID in one record raise GUID_COLLISION)

feed_text_normalization.comparison: exact code-point equality after normalization (feed_title_exact comparison)
feed_text_normalization.evidence_status: the exact feed title string is asserted by item_predicate.evidence but is not stored in a bound artefact; a mismatch fails safe (conflict, outstanding), never a false negative
feed_text_normalization.extraction: the concatenated character data of the element, as produced by the secure XML parser (parser_policy.xml): predefined entities and numeric character references resolved once, CDATA contributing ordinary character data, child elements forbidden (an element child makes the item UNIDENTIFIABLE)
feed_text_normalization.link: after normalization the link text is parsed as a URI under the frozen url_canonicalization and identity rules
not_done: NBSP (U+00A0) or other Unicode spaces are NOT converted
steps: replace every maximal run of ASCII whitespace (U+0020, U+0009, U+000D, U+000A) with one U+0020

item_predicate.known_v1_narrowness: V1 captures only statements whose feed and primary titles are exactly 'Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement'. A differently-titled FOMC action whose feed title also differs is DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE for V1 and not captured; EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO is a V1-subset assertion and never implies that no FOMC action occurred. Widening the predicate requires a spec revision.
item_predicate.no_broad_semantic_classifier: V1 must NOT be widened with keyword lists, semantic similarity, an LLM, regex over body text, or hardcoded emergency-action vocabulary. Honest incompleteness beats speculative coverage.
item_predicate.normalization: extract from parser_policy.primary_page_title_anchor, then apply parser_policy.semantic_text_normalization in its frozen order; comparison is exact and case-sensitive
item_predicate.on_positive_predicate_no_match: see primary_classification_v2: both titles non-matching -> DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE (healthy); a single match -> CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT (outstanding)

primary_classification_v2.inputs: the feed title recorded at the item's LIVE candidate birth (or the manifest entry for backfill observations) and the primary title anchor of the observation, both normalized
primary_classification_v2.non_statement_template: that routine non-statement monetary pages carry the frozen title anchor is EXPECTED but NOT EVIDENCED (the DOM evidence covers statement pages only). A non-statement page without the title anchor is PARSER_FAILED and stays outstanding until a later LIVE observation or an operator resolution concludes it.

outcomes.CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT: exactly one of the feed title and the primary title equals its exact string; UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE, outstanding
outcomes.DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE: the primary title anchor extracts successfully, primary title != primary_page_title_exact AND feed title != feed_title_exact (backfill: primary title != exact). This is a HEALTHY negative classification for the V1 subset, not a failure.
outcomes.IN_SCOPE_V1: feed title == feed_title_exact AND primary title == primary_page_title_exact AND the date anchor succeeds (for backfill observations the manifest entry replaces the feed-title conjunct)
outcomes.PARSER_FAILED: the title anchor fails, or the page would be IN_SCOPE_V1 but the date anchor fails, or any earlier processing stage fails

primary_classification_v2.scope_honesty: DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE is scoped to the frozen V1 predicate: a differently-titled FOMC action with a non-matching feed title is outside V1 and not captured. EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO never claims more than the V1 subset (zero_assertion.semantic_scope).

item_predicate.role: POSITIVE CLASSIFIER FOR THE V1 SUBSET ONLY - a non-match is NOT proof that an item is not an FOMC monetary-policy event
item_predicate.rule: CONJUNCTION - both must hold, on verified official fields only
item_predicate.superseded_rule: rev2 said a non-match was "NOT an FOMC event" - a definitive negative that allowed a false zero. Withdrawn in rev3.

HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.logical_release_metadata: SUPPORTED when the strict parser succeeds

LIVE.logical_release_metadata: SUPPORTED when the strict parser succeeds

mode_capabilities.no_blanket_flag: there is deliberately no ambiguous "retrospective supported" boolean anywhere in this spec

HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.discovery: surfaces.backfill_manifest (HISTORICAL_BACKFILL_MANIFEST_V1) only; URLs never synthesised from dates; no archive/calendar crawl
HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.raw_first: the manifest artefact is persisted durably before any backfill request
HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.relabelling: a backfill item is NEVER relabelled LIVE

modes.live_not_preempted: a backfill observation never suppresses LIVE discovery: an item seen only through HISTORICAL_BACKFILL is a NEW_FEED_CANDIDATE when the LIVE feed first lists it (item_predicate.feed_item_classification_v2), is LIVE-acquired, LIVE-anchored and linked to the existing revision
modes.mode_is_per_observation: observation_mode belongs to each per-response record and each EventRevision (from its source observation). Logical source identity is mode-neutral; an item is never labelled BACKFILL or LIVE as a whole.
modes.reconstruction: observed_at is NEVER reconstructed from source timestamps in either mode

normalized_field_notes.canonical_source_url: the existing normalized field carries canonical_primary_statement_url = the normalized official discovery link BEFORE primary redirects; it is not final_response_url or HTML canonical. No schema rename or expansion.
normalized_field_notes.capture_scope_id: binds the deterministic V1 capture subset so downstream cannot confuse provider family with coverage completeness
normalized_field_notes.classification_state: IN_SCOPE_V1 for any admitted revision; the other states never produce a revision
normalized_field_notes.declared_release_at: provider release metadata; NEVER a revision visibility gate
normalized_field_notes.official_statement_date: required normalized metadata of the observed content revision, NEVER logical identity. Date authority and validation remain timestamps.source_date; a date parse failure follows the existing parser/source-health policy. Removing the identity role does not make the date optional.
normalized_field_notes.source_item_id: stable logical identity from provider_id, event_family and the current canonical_primary_statement_url only; official_statement_date is separate revision metadata

anchor_cardinality_failure.distinction: STRUCTURAL extraction failure of the TITLE or DATE anchor - absent or duplicated - is PARSER_FAILED. Release-line anchor failures (absent, duplicated, empty or multiple declarations) are NON-GATING RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED under timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax. A successful unique title extraction that merely differs from the expected title keeps the FIX2 classification/conflict semantics.
anchor_cardinality_failure.zero_policy: a title (or, for an otherwise IN_SCOPE page, date) anchor failure concludes PARSER_FAILED; the item stays an OUTSTANDING_RELEVANT_ITEM and blocks zero. A broken template can never mean "no FOMC statement".

anchor_drift_policy.historical_templates: NO claim is made that these anchors hold for 2015, 2019, all Federal Reserve history or all monetary pages. Pages whose TITLE or DATE anchors do not match FAIL CLOSED; a non-matching release-line anchor is non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED. FIX10 adds no legacy selector.
anchor_drift_policy.immediate_release_note: no 'For immediate release' page was captured in the evidence sample, so its DOM placement is not empirically exercised. If it appears in the SAME frozen p.releaseTime anchor the existing grammar applies; otherwise the release line is non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax), never a guess.
anchor_drift_policy.on_cardinality_violation: TITLE or DATE anchor: FAIL CLOSED / PARSER_FAILED. RELEASE-LINE anchor: non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax).
anchor_drift_policy.rationale: intentional provider drift detection: if upstream markup changes, V1 must stop rather than guess

parser_policy.determinism: operates offline on verified locally stored raw body bytes and the persisted relevant HTTP Content-Type provenance required by text_decoding_v1; the same bytes, metadata and CaptureSpec hash must yield the same decoded text or PARSER_FAILED. No network or machine-dependent charset selection.

html_semantic_anchors.superseded: rev10 listed three bare names ("official statement date", "page title / event family", "release line") with no DOM authority, which R10 found could make two conforming implementations classify every statement oppositely

html_semantic_region.layout_classes_not_required: the observed heading container also carried col-xs-12 col-sm-8 col-md-8. Those are presentational and are NOT required; only the heading class token is.
html_semantic_region.relation_justification: the evidence records the full observed path div#article / div.heading.col-xs-12.col-sm-8.col-md-8 / {h3.title | p.article__time | p.releaseTime} on 5/5 pages, so the DIRECT_CHILD relation is what the evidence proves and is not a strengthening beyond it.

parser_policy.identity_url_input: supplied by identity.identity_url_authority from durable official discovery provenance; never parsed from primary HTML as a semantic anchor. HTML canonical handling is identity.html_canonical_role.
parser_policy.llm: FORBIDDEN anywhere in ingestion - an LLM may not decide whether something is an FOMC statement, nor its date, release time, identity, revision or source authority

official_statement_date_anchor.duplicate_rule: even two identical duplicate dates are structural ambiguity -> PARSER_FAILED; no value-based dedupe
official_statement_date_anchor.identity_role: UNCHANGED - remains revision metadata and NON-IDENTIFYING per FIX3
official_statement_date_anchor.last_update_negative_control: div#lastUpdate sits OUTSIDE div#article (observed directly under div.row), so it is structurally separable. Its DISPLAYED VALUE equalled the statement date on all 5 samples, so only STRUCTURE can distinguish them - a value check never could.

official_statement_date_determinism.failure: PARSER/NORMALIZER DETERMINISM FAILURE is a diagnostic, not a new global source-health state. FAIL CLOSED for parser/spec inconsistency or corruption: no second content revision, no silent normalized mutation; existing raw and immutable revisions remain intact.
official_statement_date_determinism.rule: identical verified persisted primary raw body bytes under the SAME CaptureSpec hash MUST yield identical official_statement_date metadata. A differing date with the same verified body hash is not an upstream content revision.

primary_page_title_anchor.comparison: exact string comparison against "Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement" after the frozen normalization pipeline. No contains, startswith, endswith, case-insensitive, fuzzy match or prefix-stripping heuristic.
primary_page_title_anchor.document_title_negative_control: the HTML document <title> is NOT the classifier authority on two independent evidenced grounds: its observed text is "Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement", which is PREFIXED and fails the exact predicate; and the selector is NOT UNIQUE - every sampled page carried a second <title>Lock</title> inside an inline SVG banner icon. A generic <title> lookup is therefore forbidden.
primary_page_title_anchor.document_title_permitted_use: diagnostics/provenance only; it can neither satisfy nor break the classifier

release_line_anchor.character_references: resolved to Unicode as part of extraction, BEFORE NFC; extraction never extends through later markup because descendant text exists
release_line_anchor.duplicate_rule: two p.releaseTime start tags -> RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (non-gating, timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax) even if their text is identical; no first/last wins
release_line_anchor.empty_leading_segment: if the unique start tag exists but no non-whitespace semantic character data precedes the first subsequent markup token: RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (non-gating, timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax). No fallback to descendant text and no later scan of the page.
release_line_anchor.multiple_declarations_in_segment: the single extracted segment must satisfy exactly one strict release declaration grammar; ambiguous or multiple independent declarations -> RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (non-gating, timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax), never first-match selection.
release_line_anchor.observed_result: only the release declaration plus its surrounding raw whitespace; the <ul> and everything after it is excluded
release_line_anchor.text_extent_rule: after locating the UNIQUE p.releaseTime START TAG in the decoded HTML token stream, release_line_source_text is the concatenation of the contiguous character-data / character-reference-derived text immediately following that start tag and preceding the FIRST subsequent HTML markup token. That first markup token terminates the segment.
release_line_anchor.tokenization_requirement: no parser library is pinned, but deterministic HTML tokenization sufficient to distinguish START TAG, CHARACTER DATA, CHARACTER REFERENCE and the next MARKUP TOKEN is required. Comments, declarations and tags after the start tag all terminate the segment. A parser that has already repaired the DOM in a way that loses this original token boundary may NOT substitute repaired .textContent. A tokenizer/event stream or an equivalent structural scan over the decoded HTML is acceptable provided these semantics are exact.
release_line_anchor.why_token_bound:
the evidence shows p.releaseTime is NEVER CLOSED: there is no

Token-bounded extraction removes all dependence on whether a parser closes the paragraph.

semantic_text_normalization.entity_before_nfc: character-reference resolution occurs BEFORE NFC. "é" resolves to U+0065 U+0301 and then NFC yields the canonical composed form where applicable. NFC-first is FORBIDDEN: it would leave a reference-encoded decomposed sequence unnormalized and make the classifier outcome order-dependent.
semantic_text_normalization.evidence_note: h3.title and p.article__time were already clean ASCII on 5/5 samples; only the release leading segment carried trailing LF and multiple spaces, so collapse and trim are REQUIRED there. NFC, NBSP and character references were NOT exercised by the sample - the pipeline is frozen for determinism, not because the sample demonstrated a need.
semantic_text_normalization.nbsp_rule: U+00A0 is NOT in the ASCII whitespace set. " " resolves to U+00A0 and is NOT collapsed to U+0020 by this pipeline. No browser-layout whitespace equivalence is introduced.
order: 1. HTML_CHARACTER_REFERENCE_RESOLUTION_DURING_FIELD_EXTRACTION - extract text ONLY from the frozen field-specific source: for title and date the semantic text of the unique authoritative node; for release the token-bounded leading segment defined above
2. UNICODE_NFC
3. COLLAPSE_ASCII_WHITESPACE_TO_U0020 - every maximal run of one or more ASCII whitespace code points becomes exactly one U+0020
4. TRIM_U0020 - trim leading and trailing U+0020
5. FIELD_SPECIFIC_EXACT_COMPARE_OR_STRICT_PARSE

normalization_order: 1. extract the charset/encoding value under its metadata syntax, removing syntax-level quoting only where that syntax permits it: HTTP parameter double quotes, XML attribute single/double quotes, HTML attribute single/double quotes; unquoted values remain allowed only where their metadata syntax allows them

2. trim only surrounding ASCII whitespace permitted by that metadata syntax; the possible characters are U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D and U+0020, restricted to those the relevant syntax permits. Do not trim Unicode whitespace or alter internal label characters
3. map ASCII A-Z to a-z only; no Unicode case folding or normalization
4. accept if and only if the entire resulting label is exactly utf-8 or utf8; both name the single UTF-8 codec. Every other, empty or malformed label fails with PARSER_FAILED

triggers: any recognized charset declaration is non-UTF-8, unknown, empty or malformed
a leading UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM is present
the body is not strict UTF-8
required replay charset provenance is missing rather than recording actual header absence
failure.zero_policy: This failed response cannot establish EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO. A failed discovery feed or affected primary candidate blocks zero under the existing completeness/unresolved-candidate rules. No broader source-health redesign.

forbidden: browser, locale or platform default encoding
a second decoding attempt with another codec
first-wins or last-wins selection among charset declarations

html_charset_policy.meta_charset_role: A recognized meta charset attribute is a consistency constraint, never a decoder selector. Validate every such declaration, not just the first or last.
html_charset_policy.meta_http_equiv_role: Recognize meta http-equiv=Content-Type with charset parameters in its content attribute as charset consistency signals. Match HTML attribute names and the http-equiv Content-Type value ASCII case-insensitively. Validate all charset values using the same label policy; this adds no semantic extraction or malformed-HTML recovery policy.
html_charset_policy.multiple_declarations: ALL recognized declarations must resolve to UTF-8. UTF-8 plus utf8 is compatible; UTF-8 plus windows-1252, another encoding or an unknown label fails. No declaration overrides another.

http_charset_policy.absent_parameter: No HTTP charset signal; do not synthesize a default from HTTP libraries. The sole V1 default remains UTF-8.
http_charset_policy.role: CONSISTENCY_CONSTRAINT_ONLY - every charset parameter in the persisted Content-Type values must resolve to UTF-8 under charset_label_policy. Multiple values must all agree on UTF-8; no first-wins/last-wins rule and no alternate decoder selection.

inputs: verified complete admitted body bytes, unchanged including any BOM
exact persisted relevant HTTP Content-Type field values or recorded actual header absence, as required by raw_policy.content_type_charset_provenance
the exact CaptureSpec hash bound to the revision
offline_replay.missing_metadata: FAIL CLOSED / PARSER_FAILED if required charset provenance was not preserved; never confuse missing provenance with an HTTP header that was actually absent, and never refetch metadata
offline_replay.rule: Same verified body bytes plus the same persisted relevant HTTP metadata plus the same CaptureSpec hash MUST produce the same Unicode text or the same PARSER_FAILED. No network, browser, locale, platform encoding default or machine-dependent codec alias lookup.

order: 1. complete the unchanged bounded HTTP body admission, durable raw-byte persistence and hashing; charset work never precedes these gates, and replay verifies those same stored bytes
2. the codec is already fixed to UTF-8, never inferred. Inspect the leading byte signature under utf8_bom and validate every persisted HTTP charset signal; any incompatible signal fails closed
3. form a text-only view omitting exactly one leading UTF-8 signature if present; strictly decode the entire remaining body as UTF-8 without fallback or lossy error handling

4. validate all recognized XML declaration or HTML meta charset signals on this strict UTF-8 text under the corresponding policy. This validation cannot switch codecs or trigger another decoding attempt; any incompatible declaration rejects the text

5. only after the entire charset/UTF-8 gate passes may text be supplied for XML/HTML semantic extraction and normalization. No semantic parser may override the codec or re-detect encoding from the original bytes
text_decoding_v1.scope_boundary: UTF-8 ONLY is a deliberately narrow V1 admission policy, not a claim that every Federal Reserve document uses UTF-8. FIX9 adds no Unicode NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD or NBSP/whitespace transformation: after removing the one encoding signature, decoded code points are left to the unchanged existing parser policy. XML entities/DTD/expansion, malformed HTML recovery, HTTP status/304, retries, rate windows, scheduler, recheck anchor, restart/overdue handling and timeouts are not redesigned here.
text_decoding_v1.signal_combination: There is no charset precedence competition. Zero recognized signals selects the explicit UTF-8 default. Otherwise EVERY present recognized signal must resolve to UTF-8; any unsupported, unknown or conflicting declaration causes PARSER_FAILED even when the body bytes are otherwise valid UTF-8. A declaration may constrain admission but may never select another decoder.
text_decoding_v1.strict_utf8_semantics: Decode valid UTF-8 Unicode scalar values only. Reject invalid or truncated sequences, stray/invalid continuation bytes, overlong encodings, encoded surrogate code points and values above U+10FFFF. No skipping, replacement, surrogateescape, guessed codec or second attempt.

utf8_bom.position: absolute body-byte offset 0 only, before text decoding
utf8_bom.rule: One leading EF BB BF is a UTF-8 encoding signature compatible with the sole codec. Omit exactly those three bytes from the text-only decoding view so that signature is not exposed as U+FEFF. Never mutate persisted/hash/replay bytes; the BOM still counts toward the existing decoded-body byte cap. Do not strip another BOM or any later U+FEFF code point. A non-UTF-8 declaration still causes failure even with a UTF-8 BOM.
utf8_bom.unsupported_prefix_action: PARSER_FAILED - never select UTF-16 or UTF-32; inspect the listed four-byte prefixes before the overlapping two-byte prefixes

xml_charset_policy.declaration_role: An encoding value in the XML declaration is a consistency constraint under charset_label_policy, not permission to select an XML library's own decoder. Non-UTF-8 or unknown declarations fail even if the bytes happen to be valid UTF-8/ASCII.

xml.external_entity_resolution: MUST BE DISABLED - see xml_security_policy for the full frozen set; this clause alone was found insufficient by R11
xml.security_policy_ref: parser_policy.xml_security_policy (FIX11) - authoritative and broader than the external-entity clause below
xml.unsupported_extensions: ignored unless frozen by a spec revision
xml.xxe_note: XML external entity expansion and network entity resolution are a security requirement, not an optimisation

xml_security_detection.malformed_security_syntax: malformed XML attempting to express a DOCTYPE, entity or XInclude construct falls under the existing malformed-XML policy: PARSER_FAILED, with no repair or fuzzy parsing.
xml_security_detection.rule: detection must follow XML syntactic/token semantics well enough to avoid false positives. A literal "<!DOCTYPE" or "<xi:include" appearing inside an XML COMMENT or CDATA section is not itself a prohibited construct: "<!-- <!DOCTYPE rss> -->" must NOT be rejected merely because the character sequence occurs in comment text. This keeps FIX11 from encouraging unsafe regex parsing.

body_limit_relation.what_the_caps_bound: PARSER INPUT SIZE - decoded HTTP entity-body bytes, enforced incrementally during production per FIX8
body_limit_relation.what_the_caps_do_not_bound: semantic output an XML parser could generate afterwards through DTD, entity or XInclude processing. FIX11 must NOT be read as relying on the body cap for that, and the body cap must NOT be described as bounding parser expansion.

xml_security_policy.doctype_rule: any XML document containing a DOCTYPE declaration is INVALID for FOMC V1 - <!DOCTYPE rss>, <!DOCTYPE rss [...]>, <!DOCTYPE rss SYSTEM "...">, <!DOCTYPE rss PUBLIC "...">. All are PARSER_FAILED. No partial acceptance, no "ignore the DTD and continue", no library-default decision.
xml_security_policy.external_dtd_rule: external DTD retrieval or resolution is forbidden independently of the DOCTYPE ban: no HTTP or HTTPS fetch, no file read, no local URI, no catalog lookup, no custom resolver. A document referencing an external DTD is PARSER_FAILED with NO resource access attempted.
xml_security_policy.external_entity_rule: external general entities and external parameter entities are forbidden: no resolution, no substitution, no external DTD chaining, no network and no local filesystem access. This is stated explicitly rather than left to parser defaults.
xml_security_policy.fail_before_resource_resolution: a prohibited construct must be detected and rejected WITHOUT first resolving it. <!DOCTYPE rss SYSTEM "https://evil.invalid/test.dtd"> must be rejected without fetching that URI, and file:///etc/passwd must never be opened.
xml_security_policy.internal_dtd_subset_rule: forbidden automatically because DOCTYPE is forbidden; no custom entity expansion path exists
xml_security_policy.internal_entity_expansion: NO PERMITTED PATH. Because DOCTYPE is forbidden, no user-defined internal entity can be declared, so the billion-laughs family is rejected at the DOCTYPE gate BEFORE any expansion occurs. V1 therefore needs no entity-count, nesting-depth or expanded-byte cap: the declaration machinery is simply not admitted.
xml_security_policy.network_free_parsing: after the HTTP body is durably available, parsing performs ZERO network requests, DNS lookups, filesystem reads, external catalog lookups or URI dereferences. The only parser input is the verified persisted XML body plus already-persisted metadata the CaptureSpec allows.

numeric_character_references.note: numeric character references remain permitted subject to valid XML and Unicode semantics

xml_security_policy.parser_library_independence: no library is pinned. Any library is acceptable only if configured or enveloped so these frozen semantics hold. LIBRARY DEFAULTS ARE NOT AUTHORITATIVE: an implementation must explicitly ensure DOCTYPE is rejected and that external entities, external DTDs, parameter entities, XInclude and any network/local resolver are unavailable.

predefined_xml_entities.note: the five built-in XML entity references are NOT custom DTD entity declarations and remain valid under normal XML parsing. FIX11 must not reject them.

xml_security_policy.rejection_timing: XML security checks occur BEFORE feed semantic extraction can be considered successful. A document rejected for DOCTYPE, an entity feature, XInclude or an external-resource mechanism yields NO feed items, NO candidate classification and NO EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO; its record is FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL with channel-level PARSER_FAILED, so feed polling continues.
xml_security_policy.replay: offline replay produces exactly the same result: DOCTYPE present -> PARSER_FAILED; XInclude present -> PARSER_FAILED; external entity syntax -> PARSER_FAILED. No network or local-file attempt, so replay never becomes dependent on machine filesystem contents.
xml_security_policy.second_pass_rule: after the initial parse, no resolve_entities, xinclude/process_xinclude, load_dtd, validate-against-external-DTD or any equivalent second pass that can expand or fetch resources may run. No optional parser feature may re-enable prohibited behaviour later.
xml_security_policy.stage: a deterministic PARSER-SECURITY GATE. The body has already passed the HTTP decoded-body cap, raw durability/hashing and the UTF-8 policy under the unchanged raw-first order; FIX11 changes none of those steps.
xml_security_policy.xinclude_rule: XInclude processing must never be invoked, and no inclusion of http://, https://, file://, a relative local path or any other URI may occur. Presence of the XInclude namespace or include construct in the discovery document is PARSER_FAILED. It is deliberately NOT left as an inert unknown element, because that would let different libraries behave differently.

retry_policy.feed_retry_binding: a failed feed poll is followed only by the next poll under revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.live_feed_cadence

provider.revision_support: UPSTREAM UNKNOWN - handled client-side by content-hash re-observation, never by assuming immutability

active_prior_start_rule.candidate: t is the proposed PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START instant in the current limiter epoch monotonic domain; s ranges over prior admitted starts in that same domain.
active_prior_start_rule.equal_timestamp_prior: A previously granted start at the same t cannot permit another start: provider-wide atomic registration makes it the previous_start and t - previous_start = 0 fails the mandatory spacing test.
active_prior_start_rule.exact_comparisons: A prior start of age exactly 60 seconds is excluded; age strictly below 60 and strictly above zero is included. Do not round a candidate across either the window or spacing threshold or apply an early-admission tolerance.
active_prior_start_rule.post_admission_property: For every admitted start t, the interval (t-60s,t] contains at most six admitted PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START events.

atomic_steps: 1. Inspect the current provider-wide admitted-start history and obtain candidate monotonic instant t for this decision.
2. Test count({s in history | 0 < t - s < 60}) <= 5.
3. Test t - previous_start >= 10, or pass spacing if no previous admitted start exists in this epoch.
4. Only if all preconditions and both tests pass, atomically grant, consume exactly one unit and register t in window/spacing history before another candidate can be granted.
5. Immediately initiate this attempt through the transport; no DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP side effect precedes registration.
admission.cancel_after_grant: The consumed unit is not refunded even if cancellation occurs before network I/O. Its t remains in the rolling-window and spacing histories under their normal age rules; no successful SourceObservation or EventRevision is implied.
admission.failed_admission: No grant means no physical attempt start, no network side effect and no consumed unit; pending work may be considered again when all conditions permit.
admission.immediate_initiation: A grant is not a detachable permit. It belongs to one immediate physical-attempt initiation. If the task cannot proceed after grant, abandon that authorization while keeping its consumed start; a future attempt must obtain a fresh admission. Waiting, rescheduling or another epoch cannot revive a previous grant.
admission.preconditions: Request/URL validation and any waiting precede the grant. Exclusive provider ownership and elapsed_since_limiter_epoch_begin >= 60 MUST hold before a candidate can be granted.
admission.semantic_instant: The atomic provider-limiter grant-and-consume event immediately before transport invocation for ONE validated request. This is the SAME event/timestamp for physical accounting, rolling-window history and start-to-start spacing; neither response completion nor socket write supplies a separate rate timestamp.

algorithm.alternative_algorithms: FORBIDDEN - no fixed UTC/calendar-minute bucket, token bucket or leaky bucket; no calendar-minute reset.

candidate_59_999.verdict: WAIT - both window and spacing fail; no start and no accounting unit consumed.

boundary_examples.time_origin: Unless an example explicitly uses epoch elapsed e, t=0 is an arbitrary origin AFTER the current epoch cold-start embargo, with exclusive ownership already established. Example starts at t=0 do not bypass startup embargo.

category_rules.feed_primary: Feed start at 100 and immediate statement discovery cannot permit primary start before 110, subject also to the rolling window.
category_rules.historical: Historical provider capture under this same CaptureSpec/client follows the identical limiter and has no separate capacity or fast lane.
category_rules.reattempt: Existing polling.retry_policy is unchanged. Each legitimately permitted later attempt obtains a fresh admission; no hidden transport retry or free retry.
category_rules.recheck: Being due grants no immediate network permission. Recheck work waits until limiter conditions pass; which eligible work takes a grant is frozen by revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.selection.
category_rules.redirect: Every validated redirect-follow GET independently reacquires this same rolling-window, start-spacing, monotonic and atomic provider gate; no immediate auto-follow bypass.

clock.rule: All live window, spacing and embargo elapsed comparisons use one comparable monotonic domain within the limiter epoch. Wall UTC remains recorded request/observation provenance under existing causal semantics only; it cannot accelerate or reset rate admission.

concurrency.ownership_failure: If exclusive provider admission ownership cannot be established, no provider network attempt may start. Fail closed operationally without adding a source-health enum.
concurrency.rule: All concurrent FOMC V1 emitters, including multiple processes, must share the same provider-wide atomic admission semantics and comparable current-epoch history. A centralized issuer or coordinated interprocess admission may provide this; category/process separation cannot create independent capacity. No mutex, async lock, database, file lock or IPC primitive is prescribed.
concurrency.simultaneous_workers: With five active prior starts and spacing otherwise permitting, at most one simultaneous candidate is admitted first. After its registration the other candidate MUST evaluate updated state; a same-instant candidate fails spacing with delta zero. No simultaneous provider starts.

limiter_epoch.after_embargo: Current-epoch history is empty before its first admitted start. At elapsed 60 seconds, embargo passes; normal rolling-window and spacing admission then applies. Subsequent starts update the fresh monotonic history.
applies_on: provider limiter recreation with a fresh non-comparable monotonic epoch
limiter_epoch.definition: One continuous provider runtime epoch in which all admitted-start monotonic history is available and comparable in one domain.
limiter_epoch.epoch_begin: The new admission epoch begins only after exclusive provider ownership is established and previous independent issuers can no longer initiate provider attempts. Time waiting while an old independent issuer retains emission authority cannot count toward the new epoch embargo.
limiter_epoch.no_cross_epoch_reconstruction: Do not compare or reuse precise prior-epoch monotonic timestamps for admission. No precise elapsed history is reconstructed from a new epoch. Safety uses exclusive provider ownership plus the FULL 60-second embargo measured in the NEW epoch.
limiter_epoch.ownership_continuity: A new process must not wait out an embargo in parallel with an independently active old issuer and then begin a separate budget. Ownership must exclude overlapping independent admission epochs; if that cannot be established, no new provider attempt. A fresh non-comparable epoch after ownership is re-established receives its full embargo.
limiter_epoch.safety_argument: Exclusive handoff prevents further starts from the old epoch. After 60 new-epoch monotonic seconds every unknown prior-epoch start is at least 60 seconds old and outside the strict-left rolling window. The embargo also exceeds the 10-second spacing requirement; no cross-epoch timestamp comparison or durable request-start history is required.
limiter_epoch.wall_utc_shortcut: FORBIDDEN - UTC history, persisted request times or an apparent long downtime cannot shorten or bypass the embargo.

rate_limiter.scope_boundary: FIX15 freezes the complete provider rate-admission contract only. Scheduling, overdue/coalescing/fairness (revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler), the physical-attempt deadline (http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline), source-health classification (source_health) and EST/EDT labels (timestamps.release_time.zone_label_policy) are frozen by FIX18 without changing any rate-admission rule.

spacing.completion_time_role: NONE - completion time does not set or shift the spacing reference. A starts at 0, completes at 45, B candidate at 45: spacing passes with delta 45, subject to the rolling-window condition. No completion + 10 rule.
spacing.no_previous_start: Spacing passes when current-epoch history has no admitted start; exclusive ownership and cold-start embargo still MUST pass.
spacing.previous_start: The immediately previous admitted provider-wide PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START in this epoch, including a grant followed by cancellation or transport failure.

wait_semantics.description: Work remains pending; this is not a source-health classification or a new enum.
wait_semantics.earliest_eligible_start: With ownership established, pending work is constrained by epoch_begin + 60 seconds, previous_start + 10 seconds if present, and the first instant with at most five active prior starts under 0 < t - s < 60. All conditions must hold together and be evaluated against current state at admission. Eligibility is not a reservation or a promise of queue ordering/service.

raw_policy.bytes_semantics: raw_body_bytes = the entity body AFTER standard HTTP content decoding; Content-Encoding retained as metadata
raw_policy.charset: ONLY parser_policy.text_decoding_v1 applies, AFTER complete bounded body admission, durable raw persistence and byte hashing. XML and HTML use STRICT UTF-8, also the explicit default; every recognized declaration must be UTF-8-compatible. Unsupported/conflicting/unknown charset, unsupported BOM or invalid UTF-8 => PARSER_FAILED with raw/hash preserved, no EventRevision and no zero from the failed feed/candidate. No fallback or lossy decoding.
raw_policy.content_type_charset_provenance: The existing persisted Content-Type provenance MUST preserve the exact relevant received field value(s), including charset parameters, duplicates and source spelling, or explicitly record that the header was absent. Never replace them with a library-inferred default charset, keep only the media type, or discard a conflicting value. These values and the unchanged body bytes are required offline inputs to parser_policy.text_decoding_v1. Missing recorded provenance is not equivalent to actual header absence: fail closed, no metadata refetch. This clarifies existing HTTP provenance, not a new raw/EventStore schema.
raw_policy.corrupt_raw_at_replay: verified replay FAILS CLOSED (design NORMALIZED_PRESENT_RAW_CORRUPT); raw_policy.integrity_verification applies the same rule outside replay
raw_policy.hash_algorithm_note: repo primitive sha256_bytes; no second digest algorithm introduced
raw_policy.hash_is_not_vintage_proof: the raw body hash is provenance for WHAT HYPRL ACTUALLY OBSERVED AND WHEN. It does not become proof of historical content existence merely because the same normalized record also carries a declared_release_at recovered from the page.

integrity_verification.later_detection: a mismatch found after a terminal outcome exists is recorded as a separate durable integrity diagnostic (live operation only); dependent revisions are NORMALIZED_PRESENT_RAW_CORRUPT and verified snapshots depending on them fail closed
on_mismatch: no parse and no normalization from those bytes
if the record has no terminal processing outcome yet, persist CORRUPTION_FAIL_CLOSED as its terminal outcome (live operation only); an existing terminal outcome is never replaced
no network repair and no scheduler refetch triggered by the corruption (raw_policy.network_repair FORBIDDEN)
every normalized EventRevision bound to that raw hash is NORMALIZED_PRESENT_RAW_CORRUPT: verified snapshots depending on it fail closed; the revision row is not deleted or silently recomputed
a feed record found corrupt: verified replay of its discovery cycle fails closed; the durable cycle conclusion is never rewritten
integrity_verification.replay_writes: replay is read-only: it never persists outcomes or diagnostics; it fails closed
integrity_verification.rule: Every consumer of persisted raw bytes - normal post-durable processing, restart recovery, scheduler reconciliation that reads bytes, and replay - MUST verify the stored SHA-256 before use. A digest mismatch is FAIL CLOSED everywhere, not only at replay.
integrity_verification.scheduler_effect: Satisfaction derived from the record's durable metadata stands (the observation happened); corruption never re-opens an obligation and never triggers traffic.

offline_replay.digest_mismatch: FAIL CLOSED (raw_policy.corrupt_raw_at_replay): no parser, no normalized output, no zero, no repair fetch
offline_replay.hash_persist_replay_identity: admitted body bytes hashed == bytes persisted == bytes replayed (raw_policy.bytes_semantics, http_policy.decoded_body_limit_enforcement.raw_replay_preservation)

EPISODE_OPEN, TRANSPORT_INVOKED, outcome, EPISODE_SUCCEEDED/SUSPENDED, operator and manifest records (retry_policy, zero_assertion.operator_resolution, surfaces.backfill_manifest)
processing outcome, feed item conclusion and cycle conclusion records

per-response Date/Age lines, verdicts and observed_at (causal_predicates.replay)
