redistribution.release_guard: existing repo release policy applies unchanged
redistribution.why_stricter_than_evidence: the Federal Reserve disclaimer states that, unless otherwise indicated, Board website information is in the public domain. V1 is nonetheless stricter: 6G-A does not need redistribution, and a blanket DISABLED avoids per-item 'unless otherwise indicated' rights analysis and keeps the release guard simple.

frozen_rate_semantics.restart_limiter_durability: rate_limiter.limiter_epoch: exclusive ownership plus full 60-second cold-start embargo, with no required durable prior-epoch request history

hidden_library_attempt.rule: A library MUST NOT silently perform an extra physical network attempt. Any additional attempt must be explicitly allowed by the existing policy, exposed as a distinct attempt, admitted through the same provider limiter and charged one unit. Transparent GET retries outside this policy are non-conforming; exposing/accounting for a retry alone does not authorize it.

request_accounting.logical_operation_rule: A feed poll, primary statement fetch, scheduled recheck, historical retrieval or redirecting logical fetch may produce one or more physical attempts. Each attempt consumes exactly one unit; no logical operation reserves a multi-request corridor.

preserved_policies.reobservation_anchor: revision_policy.reobservation_anchor and reobservation_anchor_timestamp_field: EXACT observed_at of the first qualifying durable primary content observation; FIX16 explicitly binds the formerly prose-only anchor.
preserved_policies.scheduler: Existing anchor, offsets, target grid and obligation identity remain unchanged. FIX17 revision_policy.reobservation_obligations freezes membership/identity/recovery; FIX18 revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler freezes status, overdue execution, coalescing, satisfaction, failed-attempt retry, completion durability and fairness.
preserved_policies.timeouts: http_policy.connect_timeout_seconds = 10 and read_timeout_seconds = 30 are unchanged. FIX18 adds http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline: a 60-second activity-independent total deadline per physical attempt.

client_max_requests_per_minute.rule: At most six PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START events in (t-60s,t] for every admitted t, under rate_limiter.algorithm and active_prior_start_rule. Prior starts count iff 0 < t - s < 60; at most five may precede the candidate. No fixed-minute reset or bucket alternative.

minimum_request_spacing_seconds.rule: Provider-wide START_TO_START: t - previous_start >= 10 seconds using the SAME PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START event as accounting/window history; equality passes and completion time is irrelevant. rate_limiter.spacing applies to every counted category with no intra-fetch exemption.

request_accounting.rate_limiter_binding: rate_limiter is authoritative for the temporal, atomic and epoch semantics of the unchanged PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START accounting unit.

reattempt.existing_policy_authority: polling.retry_policy: a later attempt is only the next feed poll or an attempt permitted by revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.retry_policy (BOUNDED_RETRY_EPISODE_V2), under the same provider ceiling.

recheck.admission_unavailable: A due recheck cannot bypass the provider accounting gate. Waiting, ordering and scheduling are frozen by revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler; FIX14 accounting is unchanged.

redirect.fourth_target_rule: If U3 returns redirect #4 after U0 plus three followed transitions, FIX12 forbids requesting U4. Four attempted requests consume four units; U4 creates no attempt and no fifth unit.
redirect.rule: After existing URL validation, every allowed target that is actually attempted MUST independently reacquire permission from the SAME provider gate BEFORE network side effects. U1 and U2 in U0 -> U1 -> U2 each require a new admission; the initial admission grants no intra-fetch exemption.

rejected_target_before_attempt.rule: A redirect Location rejected by FIX13 before network contact (including foreign host, bad scheme, forbidden query or malformed percent escape) creates no target attempt and consumes no additional unit. The request returning that redirect already consumed its own unit.

scope.category_specific_queues: MAY exist only if their aggregate physical starts are admitted through the same provider-wide limiter.
scope.historical_scope: Any historical Fed GET executed under THIS CaptureSpec V1 provider client/network policy shares this domain, one unit per physical attempt. Unrelated external research tools are outside runtime scope; no new host or URL admission is authorized.
scope.rule: All actual allowed FOMC V1 physical attempt starts belong to ONE logical provider-wide accounting/limiter domain. No separate six-per-minute feed, primary, recheck, redirect or historical quota; LIVE and HISTORICAL traffic under this same provider client share the domain.

request_accounting.scope_boundary: FIX14 accounting and FIX15 rate_limiter remain unchanged. FIX16 anchor and FIX17 obligation semantics remain unchanged. FIX18 closes scheduler execution/completion, network deadline, source-health and EST/EDT semantics through the bindings in closure_bindings; no implementation or counter-review approval is established.

source_health.attempt_failure: Existing source_health failure mappings apply if an actual attempted request later fails.
source_health.waiting_for_permission: Merely waiting for future limiter permission introduces no failure state in FIX14.

source_observation.rule: Provider-safety accounting exists even when an attempt fails before a successful response. Consuming a unit neither requires nor implies a successful SourceObservation or EventRevision; existing observation and revision semantics are unchanged.

timestamps.rule: For a successful content response, observed_at retains existing actual successful response-observation semantics; for a revision it is the successful receipt of its PRIMARY statement raw bytes. The accounting start event is not a causal timestamp replacement.

transport_substages.rule: DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP request write and response processing within ONE admitted attempt are not separate provider requests. DNS success plus TCP success plus TLS success plus one GET is one unit total. Their time bounds are frozen in http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline; accounting is unchanged.

unit.definition: One provider-accounting unit is consumed whenever the FOMC V1 client is granted permission to begin ONE concrete outbound HTTP network attempt for one already validated request URL.
unit.failure_rule: Once permission to begin the attempt is granted, its unit remains consumed even after DNS failure, TCP/connect failure, TLS failure, timeout, connection reset, read failure, a non-200 final response or any other transport failure. Accounting is tied to start authorization, never successful response.
unit.start_event_binding: rate_limiter.admission.semantic_instant: atomic grant-and-consume immediately before transport invocation, after request validation and waiting, before network side effects. The same monotonic event supplies accounting, window and spacing.

retrospective_source_fit.metadata_only_layer: a distinct metadata-only release-fact layer may be useful later, but it would need its own schema and design. This CaptureSpec does NOT invent one.
never_claims: that HyprL observed the statement historically
that the fetched bytes were the bytes visible at declared_release_at
retrospective_source_fit.retrospective_release_time_metadata: SUPPORTED - declared_release_at may be recorded as non-gating provenance
retrospective_source_fit.rule: A content-bearing revision with observation_mode = HISTORICAL_BACKFILL is NOT eligible to become source-visible at declared_release_at. It is visible only on its actual observed/durable timeline.
retrospective_source_fit.trust_policy_cannot_override: no TimestampTrustPolicyV1 verdict may substitute for missing content-vintage proof. A TRUSTED_EXACT release timestamp means "the source reliably declares the logical release at T" - it does NOT mean "every currently fetched byte existed at T".
retrospective_source_fit.validated_scope_note: explicit EST/EDT release lines were verified on SAMPLES across 2016-2026, and a "For immediate release" counterexample at 2015-03-18. V1 claims NO universal coverage. The parser is RECORD-SPECIFIC.
retrospective_source_fit.why: the historical vintage of the exact page body is not established by the verified provider contract

revision_note: Spec revision 21 (FIX20) closes the REV20 final review with a simplified runtime model: zero derives from ITEM_SEMANTICALLY_CONCLUDED item state with operator-resolution commit_seq cutoffs and per-record feed classification; PROCESSABLE (fixed at commit) governs local processing and LIVE_ELIGIBLE (own server-verified clock, reference age 0) governs every causal effect; availability, due and backoff use one server-attested time scale (92 s bound) so no local clock fault stalls capture or creates early visibility; attempts are counted by atomic durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED records and have exactly one outcome (absolute 120 bound; late responses are unverified fail-safe evidence); processing has one timer-driven owner with fenced, deadline-bounded runs; FOMC_CURRENT_CONTENT_SELECTION_V1 reads only within the commit_seq prefix P(T) of a persisted read horizon. No runtime or implementation approval.

newer_content_barrier.definition: exactly snapshot_binding.algorithm steps 3 and 6 on the prefix P(T)
newer_content_barrier.no_discard: R's raw bytes and outcome are retained; nothing is overwritten
newer_content_barrier.semantics: see snapshot_binding (states CURRENT_REVISION / CURRENT_CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_NEWER_UNNORMALIZED_SOURCE); older revisions remain immutable history
newer_content_barrier.zero: the barrier never changes any cycle conclusion

revision_policy.overwrite: FORBIDDEN - neither raw nor normalized revisions are ever overwritten
revision_policy.post_window_limitation: V1 makes NO promise to detect upstream changes after +7 days. This is an explicit, stated limitation, not an immutability claim. Extending the schedule requires CaptureSpec V2.

reobservation_anchor.causal_scope: This anchor is operational observation metadata, not proof of source content vintage. FOMC V1 content source_available_at remains null under FIX1. Raw-before-normalized visibility and observed_at semantics are unchanged; ingested_at is the server-attested avail (timestamps.ingested_at).
reobservation_anchor.clock_distinction: The anchor is canonical UTC observed_at provenance, never the FIX15 monotonic limiter-start timestamp. Monotonic comparisons remain the rate-limiter duration policy; all REV16 rate_limiter semantics are unchanged.
reobservation_anchor.declared_release_at_role: NONE as anchor authority. Earlier declared release time remains non-gating event metadata under FIX1 and cannot retroproject the observation or schedule.

durability_requirement.boundary: The existing durable raw/SourceObservation persistence boundary required for deterministic reconstruction; no new persistence primitive or EventStore schema is defined.
durability_requirement.reconstruction: After crash/restart, reconstruct the original anchor from the corresponding durable raw/SourceObservation record and its original observed_at. Raw durability time, restart time and a later normalization commit are not replacement values. Normalized EventRevision commit is not required for anchor reconstruction.
durability_requirement.rule: The supporting admitted complete raw body and observation provenance must be durable under existing primitives, retaining the original observed_at and association with the logical source item. Only then can this observation establish the persistent reobservation anchor.
durability_requirement.value_vs_survival: The anchor VALUE is observed_at; the durability boundary determines its survival/reconstructibility. These are distinct events even when their timestamp values happen to coincide.

durable_observation_before_normalized_co.rule: Once the qualifying raw/observation record is durable, preserve/reconstruct its original observed_at as anchor even if the process crashes before normalization commits.

failed_transport_attempt.rule: A consumed PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START unit does not establish an anchor. Qualifying complete primary content and its durable observation are required.

reobservation_anchor.immutability_rule: Once original anchor A is established for a logical source item, all later observations keep their own observed_at without replacing A. H1 -> H2, later raw/normalized commits, rechecks and restarts never reset the original offset grid.
reobservation_anchor.ingested_at_role: NONE as anchor authority. ingested_at is the server-attested avail of the committing transaction; it is never interchangeable with observed_at.
reobservation_anchor.logical_item_binding: The original logical source item under identity.source_item_id semantics; no new identity component or content-revision-specific anchor is introduced.
reobservation_anchor.mode_scope: Only a qualifying observation with observation_mode LIVE (a LIVE acquisition, reobservation or MANUAL_RETRY of LIVE work) can establish the anchor. HISTORICAL_BACKFILL observations never create an anchor or reobservation obligations: a current backfill fetch cannot reconstruct what changed minutes after a historical release.

non_qualifying_response.rule: A non-admitted response or incomplete/oversized aborted body cannot establish the anchor, even if transport/failure diagnostics are durable.

offset_arithmetic.precision: Instants follow timestamps.canonical_serialization (CANONICAL_UTC_TIMESTAMP_V1). A + o is computed on parsed instants at that primitive's resolution, with no truncation or rounding.
offset_arithmetic.rule: For original anchor A, targets are exactly A+300, A+3600, A+86400 and A+604800 seconds by existing canonical UTC timestamp arithmetic. Each target is computed directly from A, never from a previous actual recheck or its completion.

reobservation_anchor.offsets_binding: Exactly the unchanged revision_policy.reobservation_offsets_seconds; both representations MUST agree.

parser_failure_after_durable_raw.rule: A subsequent PARSER_FAILED or normalization failure cannot erase or move the anchor established by the qualifying durable content observation. No EventRevision success is implied. Later primary fetches of the anchored item are REOBSERVATION work under revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.

qualification.complete_admitted_body_policy: Existing bounded complete-body admission under FIX8/FIX12; no change to body production, status or raw-byte rules.
qualification.rule: ALL of final admitted HTTP 200, complete admitted primary body, its canonical observed_at and the existing durable raw/SourceObservation persistence boundary are required. Once these hold, later semantic parsing/normalization failure does not erase, postpone or replace the anchor. Anchor qualification alone admits no normalized event and does not bypass any parser, classifier, source-health or zero gate.

reobservation_anchor.rate_limiter_independence: A target is a scheduler target, not a guaranteed actual request-start time. FIX15 may delay actual admission without changing A or any future target. Missed/overdue execution, satisfaction and coalescing are frozen by revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler, never by shifting targets.
reobservation_anchor.scope_boundary: FIX16 binds anchor value, minimal durable qualification, reconstruction and the immutable offset grid. FIX17 reobservation_obligations binds the derived logical obligation set and identity. FIX18 reobservation_scheduler binds execution, satisfaction, completion durability and fairness without changing any of these.
reobservation_anchor.timestamp_definition_binding: timestamps.observed_at - unchanged actual successful receipt/observation of the complete admitted PRIMARY response body. Request initiation and response headers are not this event.
reobservation_anchor.timestamp_field_binding: revision_policy.reobservation_anchor_timestamp_field = observed_at; the timestamp_field here names exactly that same canonical field, with no alias or alternative.
reobservation_anchor.value_rule: the anchor A of S is the observed_at of S's LIVE_ELIGIBLE record with the smallest commit_seq; LIVE_ELIGIBLE is fixed at commit, so A never changes when anomalies later resolve

volatile_observation_before_durability.rule: A complete body observed only in volatile state before crash creates no surviving anchor without its required durable supporting record. Do not fabricate an anchor or obligation from memory/log inference. A later qualifying durable primary observation may establish the first persistent anchor with its own observed_at.

reobservation_closure_bindings.status: ALL_CLOSED_IN_FIX18 - every formerly open reobservation property is bound to the rule listed here

authority.rule: The sole authority for obligation membership is the existing logical source item and its original qualifying durable FIX16 anchor plus the frozen offsets. Scheduler rows cannot establish, replace or erase that anchor, add members outside its derived set, or remove members. Rows without supporting qualifying durable anchor provenance cannot create an obligation.

birth.rule: At the existing FIX16 boundary where the first qualifying primary observation makes original anchor A durably reconstructible for logical source item S, all four logical obligations exist and are required by this spec. There is no state with a qualifying durable anchor and an empty required logical set. No semantic parse success, normalized EventRevision commit or scheduler registration is an additional birth gate.

cardinality_per_source_anchor.meaning: Exactly four unique logical obligation identities across all statuses; not a count of pending/executable jobs, materialized rows or physical HTTP requests. Only the original FIX16 anchor may supply A for a given S.

crash_after_anchor_durability_before_mat.rule: Crash immediately after the qualifying anchor is durable, before any scheduler-specific write, cannot lose any logical member. Reconstruct all four original keys and A+offset targets.

crash_before_anchor_durability.rule: No obligation set is derivable from a volatile observation lost before the FIX16 durable boundary. A later first qualifying durable primary observation may establish the original anchor and its four obligations.

due_at.rule: due_at(S,A,o) = A + o seconds, directly from original observed_at under unchanged reobservation_anchor.offset_arithmetic. Recovery, materialization and execution times never shift A or any target.

reobservation_obligations.execution_and_status_binding: revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler (FIX18) is authoritative for status, satisfaction, overdue execution, coalescing, failed attempts, completion durability and fairness. FIX17 membership/identity is unchanged.

logical_identity.rule: The ordered tuple (S,A,o) is the authoritative logical identity, with S from unchanged identity.source_item_id, A exclusively the ONE original durable FIX16 reobservation anchor for S, and o one of the frozen offsets. Logical equality is equality of these three canonical values. A is not a caller-selected later observation or cache timestamp. Preserve existing canonical timestamp representation/precision; no rounding.
logical_identity.same_timestamp_distinct_source_items: S1 != S2 with identical A still yields disjoint sets of four keys, eight total.
logical_identity.storage_encoding: UNSPECIFIED - an implementation may encode/hash the tuple or use another physical row ID, but physical IDs cannot change tuple equality.

materialization.rule: Materialized membership is an optional cache/index/queue aid. With a durable anchor, zero rows, two rows, four correct rows or duplicate rows all represent the same four logical obligations. Existing rows must reconcile to derived keys and targets; missing rows do not authorize missing logical work, and conflicting cache values have no authority over the original anchor or derived set. No corruption-repair procedure or storage primitive is prescribed.
materialization.status_boundary: The cache rule concerns membership, identity and target only. Derivation/reconciliation neither assigns nor resets status, establishes satisfaction, nor authorizes execution by itself. Status is derived under revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler from durable qualifying observation records; completion rows are caches that cannot override that derivation.

reobservation_obligations.offsets_binding: Exactly revision_policy.reobservation_offsets_seconds and reobservation_anchor.offsets_seconds; all representations MUST agree.

parser_failure_after_durable_anchor.rule: A later parser/normalization failure cannot erase the four obligations entailed by a qualifying durable anchor. No parsing success or EventRevision commit is implied; execution and satisfaction follow revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.

reobservation_obligations.provenance_and_rate_boundary: Obligation keys, target times and materialization are operational metadata, not observed content or source-vintage evidence. Derivation creates no SourceObservation or EventRevision and changes no observed_at, ingested_at or source_available_at. It performs no HTTP attempt, consumes no request unit and grants no limiter permit or retry permission. Actual permitted attempts remain subject to unchanged FIX14/FIX15 and polling.retry_policy.

reconstruction.elapsed_time: All four identities remain logically derivable even when recovery occurs after one or every due_at. Their status after recovery is derived under revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.completion_durability; physical row retention is not required.
reconstruction.repeated_interrupted_concurrent_recovery: Repeated, interrupted or concurrent reconstructors derive the same four logical keys and targets. Repeated insertions or retry after a lost materialization-write ACK cannot create a fifth logical member or a second grid.
reconstruction.rule: On startup/recovery, every durable anchor governed by this V1 spec MUST yield its complete exact logical set. Discovery/derivation cannot depend on existing scheduler rows, a registration marker or a normalized EventRevision. Deterministic on-demand derivation, reconciliation/materialization or an equivalent mechanism is allowed; the resulting set is not optional.

revision_behavior.rule: H1 -> H2, repeated H1 observations, later parse success and restart preserve original S,A and the same four keys. SourceObservation multiplicity is independent of obligation-grid identity. Existing source identity and immutable raw/EventRevision semantics are unchanged.

reobservation_obligations.scope_boundary: FIX17 freezes logical obligation birth, identity, cardinality and crash reconstruction. Four logical obligations do not imply four HTTP GETs, immediate execution or exactly-once dispatch. FIX18 revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler freezes status, overdue execution, coalescing, satisfaction, failed attempts, completion durability and fairness; http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline, source_health and timestamps.release_time.zone_label_policy close the remaining network, health and EST/EDT semantics.
reobservation_obligations.spec_binding: The anchor/grid is governed by the CaptureSpec semantics recorded under existing provenance conventions. The future implementation binds records to its authoritative final spec hash. CaptureSpec hash is not added to this logical tuple. FIX17 introduces no runtime migration, cross-version reconciliation or identity churn from pre-implementation spec revisions.

revision_policy.reobservation_rationale: detects immediate, same-day, next-day and delayed corrections; ~4 extra requests per statement at roughly 8 statements a year is negligible

authority.rule: Obligation status is a deterministic function of durable records only: the durable original FIX16 anchor supplies membership (FIX17) and durable qualifying primary observation records of the same logical source item supply satisfaction. Scheduler rows, completion markers, queues and in-memory state are caches or execution aids; they cannot create, erase, satisfy or un-satisfy an obligation.

candidate_acquisition.birth: item_predicate.feed_item_classification_v2 step 4 creates the LIVE feed candidate record and exactly one LIVE_ACQUISITION per source item, committed with the classifying feed record's classification (eligible or not)
candidate_acquisition.conclusion: an acquisition concludes when a LIVE_ELIGIBLE observation of the item commits and is RECORD_PROCESSING_TERMINAL; failures follow retry_policy; SUSPENDED is not a conclusion

discovery_side_classification_input.rule: The feed title recorded at the LIVE candidate birth (normalized, FEED_TEXT_NORMALIZATION_V1) is the LIVE discovery-side input for every LIVE observation of the item; the manifest entry is the input for backfill observations. Later feed titles never re-evaluate it (feed_item_classification_v2.feed_title_change).

candidate_acquisition.durability: the acquisition record is durable required work independent of later feed observations: a later feed that omits the item never cancels it, and dispatch reads durable acquisition records, never only the latest feed

clock.due_eligibility_clock: NOW_LB (causal_predicates.SERVER_NOW_LB); no local wall or elapsed reading decides due; a wrong local clock can only delay due work, never make it early
clock.rate_admission: Unchanged FIX15 monotonic limiter; wall UTC never accelerates or resets admission.
clock.satisfaction_comparison: Satisfaction compares persisted canonical observed_at against due_at; it never uses dispatch time, monotonic time or completion-marker time.
clock.timestamp_precision: timestamps.canonical_serialization (CANONICAL_UTC_TIMESTAMP_V1); comparisons on parsed instants only
clock.wall_clock_jump: Local clock steps, suspend, pauses and boots never open, close or reopen episodes and never make work due; only durable records and verified server time do.

completion_durability.authority: satisfaction.rule evaluated over durable qualifying observation records. Nothing else establishes completion.
completion_durability.completion_rows: Optional caches. A row claiming SATISFIED without a supporting durable qualifying record has no authority; a missing or stale row cannot un-satisfy. Rows must reconcile to the derived status.
completion_durability.crash_after_observation_durable_before_m: Recovery derives SATISFIED for every obligation with due_at <= R.observed_at and commits the derivable EPISODE_SUCCEEDED records (retry_policy.terminal_records). A duplicate provider GET because a marker, cache row or outcome record was lost is FORBIDDEN.
completion_durability.crash_before_observation_durable: The volatile observation never existed for scheduling purposes. Obligations stay PENDING and a new real fetch is required and conforming; nothing is synthesized from memory or logs.
completion_durability.late_durable_record: A limiter epoch controls permission to START provider transport only. A response started under an owned epoch whose record commits after an epoch transition is a normal observation if its attempt still has no outcome, otherwise LATE_EVIDENCE (durable_ordering.late_durable_record); live derivation and replay treat it identically. After ownership loss the old issuer MUST NOT start another physical attempt (FIX15).
completion_durability.raw_corruption: Scheduler derivation reads durable per-response metadata and does not re-verify body digests. Raw corruption is handled by raw_policy.corrupt_raw_at_replay (fail closed) and NEVER triggers a repair refetch (raw_policy.network_repair FORBIDDEN).
completion_durability.recovery_rule: At epoch start and on every reconciliation trigger, derive obligation status from durable records, commit INTERRUPTED outcomes and any derivable EPISODE_SUCCEEDED records, and run processing reconciliation before dispatching work of the affected item.

execution.after_final_satisfaction: Once O604800 is satisfied, S generates no further reobservation traffic (revision_policy.post_window_limitation).
execution.dispatch: One dispatch of S = one logical fetch of S's stored canonical_primary_statement_url (identity.reobservation_identity_stability) with at most 3 followed redirects; every physical attempt independently obtains FIX15 admission.
execution.no_catch_up_burst: Several overdue obligations of S never produce back-to-back GETs. After a qualifying R, obligations with due_at <= R.observed_at are satisfied by it and later ones wait for their own due_at.
execution.not_due: An item with only PENDING_NOT_DUE obligations is never fetched as reobservation work.
execution.post_anchor_primary_fetch_routing: Once S has a LIVE anchor, LIVE discovery never issues a primary GET for S; feed relisting causes no primary request. Every further LIVE primary GET of S is REOBSERVATION work. HISTORICAL_BACKFILL manifest entries are separate BACKFILL_ENTRY work.
execution.work_unit: REOBSERVATION work is per open REOBSERVATION episode of a LIVE-anchored item S. It is eligible iff its next attempt is eligible (retry_policy), no logical fetch of S is in flight, and every PROCESSABLE record of S is RECORD_PROCESSING_TERMINAL (bounded by run deadlines).

fairness.dead_items: dead items consume at most one bounded episode per key and are then EPISODE_SUSPENDED and ineligible; they can never consume the budget indefinitely
fairness.fresh_work: a fresh obligation's first attempt is eligible once it is PENDING_DUE (NOW_LB >= due_at + 92) and is never behind retries whose next eligible instant is later; restart never resets keys (they derive from durable outcome records)
fairness.guarantee: While FIX15 keeps granting, a class with eligible work is selected within every run of consecutive contested decisions whose length is the number of classes with eligible work, across restarts (rotation derives from durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED records). Within a class, an eligible episode is overtaken only by episodes with a smaller (next eligible instant, source_item_id) key; each attempt moves its episode's key forward by at least 60 s or ends it, and suspended episodes are never eligible, so every eligible episode is served after finitely many decisions. Within FEED_DISCOVERY, feed polls and LIVE acquisitions alternate durably. HISTORICAL_BACKFILL orders first by manifest record (commit_seq), so within that class service is finite but manifest-ordered.

grid_immutability.rule: due_at(S,A,o) = A + o always (revision_policy.reobservation_obligations.due_at). Late execution, limiter delay, failures, retries, restarts and satisfaction times never shift any target.

live_feed_cadence.feed_poll_failure: a failed poll is followed only by the next due poll; feed polls have no retry episode
live_feed_cadence.no_catch_up_polls: a delayed poll never produces extra polls
live_feed_cadence.rule: At most one feed poll is pending or in flight. The next poll becomes due 60 s after the latest feed TRANSPORT_INVOKED (boottime within a boot; immediately after the FIX15 embargo in a new boot) and only after every earlier PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record is FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL (and, if cycle-starting, has its cycle conclusion) and every earlier poll attempt has an outcome. An ineligible feed response ends its attempt without a cycle. A conclusion commit failure is local work and never triggers a new poll.

lost_ack.rule: If the durable write of R, or any later completion-cache write, succeeded but the caller lost the ACK, recovery re-reads durable state and derives the same satisfied set. No duplicate logical completion exists because status is derived. EventRevision creation stays idempotent under the (source item, content hash) key (identity.revision_id) and timestamps.ingested_at.lost_ack.
lost_ack.unknown_local_write_outcome: Resolve by reading durable state before any dispatch of S; never by refetching from the provider.

missed_and_overdue.collector_offline_across_due_at: The obligation survives restart as PENDING and, once due, is served by its own REOBSERVATION episode (retry_policy.opening_conditions) unless another episode of S is open or its own episode is SUSPENDED.
missed_and_overdue.no_historical_synthesis: The eventual reobservation is ONE real current observation with its own real observed_at. No synthetic, backdated, interpolated or historical observation is created for a missed target, and due_at is never rewritten.
missed_and_overdue.overdue_duration_irrelevant: An obligation overdue by seconds or by days follows the same rules.
missed_and_overdue.rule: Passing due_at never ends, skips, expires or fails an obligation. A PENDING_DUE obligation remains required, with no time limit, until satisfaction.rule holds.

post_durable_processing.first_terminal_outcome_authoritative: each record has exactly one terminal processing outcome: the first one committed; nothing later (including replay or a later integrity failure) replaces it
post_durable_processing.identity_conflict: IDENTITY_CONFLICT: the per-response record's request URL does not canonicalize to the identity URL of the item it is associated with, or the association itself is inconsistent; fail closed, outstanding
post_durable_processing.ingested_at: ingested_at = avail of the committing transaction (durable_ordering.commit_instant); commit retry timing is local latency and never rewrites observed_at
post_durable_processing.normalized_success: NORMALIZED success means terminal outcome NORMALIZED_REVISION_COMMITTED or NORMALIZED_SAME_CONTENT_NO_NEW_REVISION
post_durable_processing.processing_gate: No provider fetch of S is dispatched while a PROCESSABLE record of S lacks a terminal processing outcome; no feed poll is dispatched while an earlier PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record is not FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL or a cycle-starting one lacks its conclusion. Run deadlines and the poison guard bound both, so neither holds forever.
post_durable_processing.provider_traffic: NONE - post-durable processing and its retries never cause a provider request

reconciliation.authority: required local work is derived from durable records: every PROCESSABLE record without a terminal processing outcome, every cycle-starting feed record without a conclusion, every IN_SCOPE_V1 outcome whose link or conclusion is missing, and every derivable episode or attempt record
reconciliation.derivable_records: attempt outcomes (INTERRUPTED) and EPISODE_SUCCEEDED/SUSPENDED are re-derived at every trigger until committed; they never become INTERNAL_PROCESSING_ERROR
reconciliation.local_retry: within a run, a failed local commit is retried up to 3 more times, no sooner than 60 s apart (boottime); then the run is DEAD
reconciliation.no_provider_traffic: reconciliation and processing never cause a provider request
reconciliation.owner: only the current exclusive limiter-epoch owner runs reconciliation and processing; at most one RUNNING run per record
reconciliation.poison_guard: a record whose runs reached DEAD twice receives terminal INTERNAL_PROCESSING_ERROR, committed by the current owner under its epoch token (no RUNNING run required) and re-derived at every trigger until committed (fail closed; a feed record gets a NOT_ZERO conclusion if cycle-starting and becomes a failed-feed item); RUNNING runs never count
reconciliation.run_states: each run commits PROCESSING_RUN {run_id, epoch, deadline = start + 600 s monotonic} before processing; a run is RUNNING until its terminal outcome commits; at the next trigger the owner marks it DEAD when its epoch is not current, its task ended without outcome, or its deadline passed. Outcome and link commits are fenced: they commit only while their run is RUNNING in the current epoch.
triggers: a periodic tick at least every 60 s (monotonic), which also evaluates every run and attempt deadline
after every durable commit of a per-response record (including a late record from an earlier epoch)
before every scheduler decision to start a physical request

post_durable_processing.revision_creation: Processing of a qualifying record carrying H that concludes IN_SCOPE_V1 commits an observation-to-revision link; the EventRevision for (S, H) is created by the first such link (smallest commit_seq) and reused by later ones (revision_policy.revision_mode_neutrality). A hash that does not conclude IN_SCOPE_V1 creates no revision.
post_durable_processing.rule: Every durable qualifying primary observation MUST be processed to a durable conclusion (text decoding, parsing, classification and, when IN_SCOPE_V1, normalized EventRevision commit or a recorded PARSER_FAILED outcome). Processing is a deterministic offline function of the durable bytes, persisted metadata and CaptureSpec hash, and needs no network.
post_durable_processing.when: governed by reconciliation.triggers; integrity verification runs before every parse

reobservation_scheduler.provenance_and_rate_boundary: Scheduler state, eligibility, selection and derived status are operational metadata. They create no SourceObservation or EventRevision, change no observed_at, ingested_at, declared_release_at or source_available_at, and grant no limiter permit.
reobservation_scheduler.replay_role: Offline replay never runs the scheduler and needs no network. Obligation status is derivable offline from durable records.

retry_policy.attempt_classification: an attempt is SATISFYING iff a LIVE_ELIGIBLE record (for HISTORICAL_BACKFILL work: a CLOCK_VERIFIED PROCESSABLE HISTORICAL_BACKFILL record) linked to it satisfies the episode's work; every other counted attempt is NON_SATISFYING, including a LIVE_ELIGIBLE record that leaves the obligation PENDING; such records still count for processing, revisions and snapshots.
retry_policy.attempt_consumption: For every logical fetch (episode attempt or feed poll), after ownership, URL validation and the FIX15 grant, the task commits TRANSPORT_INVOKED as its last step before the first transport call. The TRANSPORT_INVOKED transaction atomically requires: the current limiter-epoch fencing token, for episode work the episode open and fewer than 6 TRANSPORT_INVOKED records for the episode, and no attempt of the same item (for a feed poll: no feed poll) without an outcome; otherwise it does not commit and nothing is sent. Transport must start within 1 s of the grant; if TRANSPORT_INVOKED has not committed by then, the grant is abandoned (FIX15 unit consumed, no network I/O) and the work gets a local non-durable hold of 60 s. Once TRANSPORT_INVOKED is durable the attempt COUNTS, whatever happens next. Selection, limiter waiting, ownership failure and validation count nothing. Redirect hops belong to the same attempt (FIX15 units each; at most 4 physical requests per attempt).

attempt_outcome_fence.consequence: attempt outcomes and LIVE_ELIGIBLE records of each item, and of the feed, commit in request order; a late response can only add fail-safe discovery and reopen state, never a conclusion, anchor, satisfaction or current content
attempt_outcome_fence.counting: LATE_EVIDENCE adds no attempt and no request: its attempt was already counted
attempt_outcome_fence.rule: every TRANSPORT_INVOKED (episode attempt or feed poll) has at most one outcome, the first committed. A per-response record commits as its attempt's outcome only while the attempt has none. A response that arrives after its attempt already has an outcome is still committed raw-first as a per-response record flagged LATE_EVIDENCE; it is not the attempt's outcome, and every rule treats it as CLOCK_UNVERIFIED: it is processed and (for the feed) classified in commit_seq order, so it may create candidates, markers and diagnostics and may reopen an item, but it is never LIVE_ELIGIBLE and never anchors, satisfies, starts a cycle, concludes an item, makes content current or serves as a clock reference for avail or NOW_LB. An attempt with an outcome receives no further FIX15 continuation grant.

retry_policy.attempt_outcome_precedence: each TRANSPORT_INVOKED has exactly one outcome, the first committed (attempt_outcome_fence); a per-response record is that outcome. The k-th attempt of an episode is its k-th TRANSPORT_INVOKED.

attempt_outcomes.qualifying: a LIVE_ELIGIBLE (or, for backfill work, CLOCK_VERIFIED PROCESSABLE backfill) record linked to the attempt

episode_keys.rule: at most one episode per key, ever; keys contain no wall time; restart, relisting, clock steps and recovery never create a key

retry_policy.episode_open: before its first attempt an episode commits EPISODE_OPEN {key, attempt_budget 6, backoff schedule, triggering work, offset where applicable, opened commit_seq} EPISODE_OPEN for an existing key, and a second LIVE_ACQUISITION for a source_item_id, are rejected by the commit (unique keys). A REOBSERVATION EPISODE_OPEN commits only if its anchor is the item's anchor record and its offset is one of the four frozen offsets.
retry_policy.first_attempt_eligibility: a new episode's first attempt is eligible when its opening condition holds and NOW_LB >= avail(latest NON_SATISFYING outcome of any episode of the same item) + 60
retry_policy.interrupted: the current exclusive limiter-epoch owner is the only authority: at every reconciliation trigger it commits INTERRUPTED for every TRANSPORT_INVOKED of a non-current epoch without a durable outcome, and for its own attempts whose task ended without an outcome or that have no outcome 600 s (monotonic) after TRANSPORT_INVOKED; an attempt whose 120 s post-network save deadline passed gets LOCAL_PERSISTENCE_FAILED instead (local_failure). INTERRUPTED attempts count. Either outcome commits only if the attempt still has none; a response arriving afterwards is LATE_EVIDENCE (attempt_outcome_fence).

local_failure.bytes_in_memory: local persistence is retried in process until the attempt's local deadline (120 s monotonic after its network phase ends); then the owner commits LOCAL_PERSISTENCE_FAILED; no network
local_failure.bytes_lost: LOCAL_PERSISTENCE_FAILED: one non-qualifying attempt of the episode (design crash_state_matrix A 'refetch', bounded)
local_failure.store_unavailable: TRANSPORT_INVOKED must commit before any network I/O, so no request can start while the store cannot commit; capture of already-running attempts is unaffected

retry_policy.local_fault_budget: CLOCK_UNVERIFIED, CLOCK_INELIGIBLE, LOCAL_PERSISTENCE_FAILED, INTERRUPTED and CANCELLED_AFTER_INVOKE outcomes count; a persistent local fault can exhaust an episode, which then needs an operator MANUAL_RETRY (fail-safe); a provider-side stale Date without Age on one item's pages has the same effect (stated residual)

manual_retry.closure: if the retried work becomes satisfied (by any LIVE_ELIGIBLE observation) before the manual episode's next TRANSPORT_INVOKED, EPISODE_SUCCEEDED (reason work_satisfied) is committed, derived before any dispatch; an in-flight manual attempt persists its observation normally and the episode then closes
manual_retry.eligibility: a MANUAL_RETRY episode is dispatchable when its retried work is unsatisfied, no fetch of the item is in flight and its next attempt is eligible per time_basis; for REOBSERVATION work the obligation must be PENDING_DUE
manual_retry.isolation: manual episodes never mutate, reopen or replace autonomous episode keys; their traffic is outside the 120 autonomous bound
manual_retry.mode: a MANUAL_RETRY observation takes the observation_mode of the retried work (LIVE for LIVE_ACQUISITION or REOBSERVATION, HISTORICAL_BACKFILL for a backfill entry)

retry_policy.no_tight_loop: minimum 60 s between attempts of one key; FIX15 bounds provider-wide rate
retry_policy.one_in_flight_per_item: at most one logical fetch per source item is in flight across all classes (LIVE_ACQUISITION, REOBSERVATION, HISTORICAL_BACKFILL, MANUAL_RETRY)

opening_conditions.HISTORICAL_BACKFILL: the manifest record exists and the entry has no episode
opening_conditions.LIVE_ACQUISITION: the acquisition record exists, has no episode, and the item has no LIVE anchor
opening_conditions.MANUAL_RETRY: the operator record exists; for REOBSERVATION work the obligation is PENDING_DUE
opening_conditions.REOBSERVATION: obligation (S, A, o) is PENDING_DUE, it has no episode, S has no other open REOBSERVATION episode, and o is the smallest offset among S's PENDING_DUE obligations without an episode

retry_policy.provider_basis: provider rate contract UNKNOWN and automated-access prohibition NOT_VERIFIED; traffic must stay finite per item

schedule.rule: after the k-th NON_SATISFYING attempt (k = 1..5, 1-based), attempt k+1 is eligible per time_basis

suspension.later_offsets: another offset has its own key and may open its own episode when due; a later success may satisfy the suspended obligation by coalescing, which commits no reopening
suspension.suspended_work: exactly the episode's own key; for REOBSERVATION the single obligation (S, A, o), which stays PENDING and auditable
suspension.wake: EPISODE_SUSPENDED is final for autonomous traffic; only a MANUAL_RETRY operator record creates further traffic for that work, under its own key and outside the autonomous bound

terminal_records.EPISODE_SUCCEEDED: committed when the episode's work is satisfied: REOBSERVATION when its obligation is SATISFIED (any LIVE_ELIGIBLE observation, including coalescing and MANUAL_RETRY); LIVE_ACQUISITION when any LIVE_ELIGIBLE record of the item commits; HISTORICAL_BACKFILL when a qualifying backfill record from one of its attempts commits; MANUAL_RETRY per retry_policy.manual_retry.closure. Derivable, and derived before any dispatch.
terminal_records.EPISODE_SUSPENDED: committed with the authoritative outcome of the 6th TRANSPORT_INVOKED when that attempt is NON_SATISFYING and the work is unsatisfied; recovery commits any derivable EPISODE_SUSPENDED (six NON_SATISFYING TRANSPORT_INVOKED, work unsatisfied, none in flight) before any dispatch
terminal_records.authority: an episode is open iff EPISODE_OPEN exists without a terminal record; the first terminal record committed is final and later ones are diagnostics. Recovery and every reconciliation trigger commit any derivable EPISODE_SUCCEEDED or EPISODE_SUSPENDED before any dispatch. No clock reading opens, closes or reopens an episode.

time_basis.never: no local wall-clock deadline or elapsed-time credit is persisted or carried across restarts; restart never creates an episode or attempt
time_basis.no_verified_time: while no verified response arrives (provider unreachable, local clock wrong by > 90 s), due and backoff decisions hold and work is never burned by waiting; an attempt already eligible when a clock fault begins (or a new acquisition's first attempt) may still be spent as CLOCK_UNVERIFIED. Raw capture, feed polling and local processing continue. Stated residual: while the feed is persistently unverified, a stuck episode neither advances nor suspends, so RESOLVE stays invalid for its item; no cycle exists then, so no false ZERO
time_basis.restart: the rule reads only durable records and server-attested time, so it is identical after restart or a new boot; the true wait is at least the backoff and, with verified feed polls, ends within about backoff + 184 s + two feed cadences with an accurate clock (up to backoff + 366 s + two cadences within the 90 s check tolerance)
time_basis.rule: attempt k+1 is eligible when NOW_LB >= avail(outcome of attempt k) + backoff[k] (causal_predicates); avail is an upper bound of the outcome's true durability and NOW_LB a lower bound of the true present, so the true wait is never shorter than the backoff

upper_bound_proof.attempts_per_key: at most 6 TRANSPORT_INVOKED records per key, enforced by the TRANSPORT_INVOKED commit itself; an attempt without one sends nothing; one with one always counts
upper_bound_proof.autonomous_keys_per_live_item: 1 LIVE_ACQUISITION + 4 REOBSERVATION (one per offset of the single LIVE anchor) = 5
upper_bound_proof.invariance: keys are unique and contain no clock value; the anchor is fixed at commit by LIVE_ELIGIBLE; terminal records are final; attempts are counted by durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED records that precede any network I/O; restart, clock anomaly or correction, suspend, relisting, operator resolution or retry, late old-epoch attempts and processing retries cannot add keys or attempts
upper_bound_proof.outside_the_bound: HISTORICAL_BACKFILL runs (operator-started, at most 1000 entries x 24 per manifest record) and MANUAL_RETRY episodes (24 each)
upper_bound_proof.store_assumption: the bound assumes the durable, serialized store (design rev4 EventStore) with fsync-durable commits; a restored, re-initialized, replaced or forked store, or commits that are not durable on power loss, are outside V1 and invalidate the bound

satisfaction.changed_content: A qualifying R with a changed body hash satisfies eligible obligations at R's durability boundary. Downstream parsing/normalization then appends the new immutable revision under existing rules. Satisfaction neither waits for nor depends on that commit, and a later normalization or commit failure cannot un-satisfy.

coalescing.example: Observation at A+4000 satisfies O300 and O3600; O86400 and O604800 stay PENDING.
coalescing.not_historical_reconstruction: Coalesced satisfaction records that the source was re-observed at R.observed_at. It does not claim or synthesize the source state at any earlier due_at.
coalescing.prefix_property: Because A+300 < A+3600 < A+86400 < A+604800, the satisfied set of S is always the offset prefix {o | A + o <= max qualifying observed_at of S}.
coalescing.rule: One qualifying R satisfies EVERY obligation of the same S whose due_at <= R.observed_at, including several overdue obligations at once. Obligations of S with due_at > R.observed_at stay PENDING. R never satisfies obligations of another source item.

satisfaction.late_execution: Lateness is not failure. A qualifying R whose observed_at is later than A+300, because of the due margin, FIX15 delay or downtime, satisfies O300. Limiter waiting is not a source failure, not a checkpoint failure, not a new anchor and not a new due_at.
satisfaction.no_early_satisfaction: R with R.observed_at < due_at satisfies nothing for that obligation, now or later; no pre-satisfaction and no carry-forward credit. Observation at 18:30 cannot satisfy O3600 due 19:00.

non_satisfying_outcomes.obligation_effect: obligation stays PENDING; provider work follows retry_policy (BOUNDED_RETRY_EPISODE_V2)
outcomes: redirect Location failure, rejection or limit exhaustion
response lost before durable per-response persistence (crash or persistence failure)
detected local persistence failure (bytes obtained, not durable)

parser_failure_after_durable_observation.source_health: PARSER_FAILED on the primary_statement surface under existing mappings
parser_failure_after_durable_observation.zero: blocked where the item is relevant under zero_assertion

qualifying_observation.definition: a LIVE_ELIGIBLE per-response record of S (causal_predicates.LIVE_ELIGIBLE); its own per-response record, not source_observation_id or EventRevision, is the satisfaction key
qualifying_observation.initiating_path: Only LIVE_ELIGIBLE records of S satisfy S's obligations, whatever work produced them (acquisition, reobservation or MANUAL_RETRY of LIVE work). HISTORICAL_BACKFILL records never do. The anchor observation satisfies nothing.
qualifying_observation.per_response_record_required: Every admitted response persists its own per-response record with its own observed_at, including a same-content response (revision_policy.unchanged_refetch). Body-byte storage MAY be shared by content hash as a storage mechanic, and the content-derived identity.source_observation_id MAY repeat; satisfaction is keyed to the per-response record, not to source_observation_id, content_hash or EventRevision.

satisfaction.rule: Obligation (S,A,o) is SATISFIED iff there exists a LIVE_ELIGIBLE record R of S with R.observed_at >= A + o (canonical instants; equality satisfies). Otherwise it is PENDING.
satisfaction.same_content: A qualifying R whose body hash equals a prior hash of S satisfies every eligible obligation under coalescing. It creates no new EventRevision (revision_policy.same_item_same_body_hash).
satisfaction.satisfying_observation_for_audit: the qualifying record of S with the smallest commit_seq among those with observed_at >= A + o; any exported or cached SATISFIED status MUST carry that record's id and observed_at so lateness (observed_at - due_at) is always visible.

selection.class_rule: select the first class with eligible work in class_cycle_order strictly after the class of the latest durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED record (largest commit_seq), wrapping around; with none, start at FEED_DISCOVERY. A class without eligible work consumes no turn. MANUAL_RETRY episodes belong to the class of their work.
selection.continuations_first: a validated redirect-follow request of an in-flight logical attempt takes the next grant before any new attempt (smallest TRANSPORT_INVOKED commit_seq first) and does not affect rotation
selection.decision_point: A selection decision happens only when a new logical fetch's initial physical attempt is about to obtain a FIX15 grant; exactly one eligible work item is selected per decision.
selection.fix15_authority: Selection chooses WHICH work takes a grant; FIX15 alone decides WHEN a grant exists.
selection.implementation_freedom: threads, queues and locks are free; the observable sequence of selected work must equal this rule
selection.rotation_state: derived from durable TRANSPORT_INVOKED records only; identical after restart
selection.within_FEED_DISCOVERY: when both a due feed poll and an eligible LIVE_ACQUISITION episode exist, alternate by the kind of the latest durable FEED_DISCOVERY TRANSPORT_INVOKED record (with none, the poll first); otherwise whichever is eligible. LIVE_ACQUISITION episodes are ordered by (next eligible instant, source_item_id).
selection.within_HISTORICAL_BACKFILL: eligible HISTORICAL_BACKFILL episodes ordered by (manifest record commit_seq, next eligible instant, source_item_id)
selection.within_REOBSERVATION: eligible episodes ordered by (next eligible instant, source_item_id, offset_seconds); the first attempt's eligible instant is retry_policy.first_attempt_eligibility
selection.work_conserving: Whenever eligible work exists and FIX15 would admit a start, a selection decision occurs and that start is made. No idling, serialization of logical fetches or concurrency cap below FIX15 and the one-in-flight rules (one feed poll, one fetch per work item).

derived_pending_views.PENDING_DUE: PENDING and NOW_LB >= due_at + 92 (causal_predicates.SERVER_NOW_LB); then every later CLOCK_VERIFIED response has observed_at >= due_at, so a verified reobservation always satisfies

status_model.enum_spelling: Physical enum names and encodings are implementation choices; the two-state semantics and derived views are not.
status_model.failure_is_not_status: Attempt failure is an attempt/source-health outcome, never an obligation status. A failed attempt neither satisfies nor destroys an obligation.
status_model.irreversibility_basis: Supporting qualifying observation records are immutable under revision_policy.overwrite; V1 defines no deletion of them.
transitions: SATISFIED is irreversible; no transition back to PENDING

work_classes.no_silent_drop: Required work is derived from durable records (anchors, obligations, acquisition records, manifests, episodes); queue pressure, restart or later feed contents never delete it.
work_classes.shared_limiter: All classes obtain every physical start from the unchanged FIX15 provider-wide limiter; no independent budget.

revision_mode_neutrality.availability: the availability of a revision through a given observation is that link's avail (>= its observed_at); a revision is available at T iff it has a CLOCK_VERIFIED link within P(T); LIVE availability requires a LIVE_ELIGIBLE link
revision_mode_neutrality.backfill_then_live: BACKFILL H1 creates V1; a later LIVE H1 observation links to V1 (no duplicate) and makes V1 LIVE-available from that link's availability instant
revision_mode_neutrality.design_field: design rev4 per_revision_fields.observation_mode is kept on the revision as CREATION PROVENANCE ONLY (the mode of the observation that created it); it has no gating or admissibility role for FOMC
revision_mode_neutrality.rule: An EventRevision is keyed by (source item, content hash) and is mode-neutral. Each PROCESSABLE observation whose processing concludes IN_SCOPE_V1 commits an observation-to-revision link (creating the revision if it does not exist). The link carries the observation's observation_mode and observed_at and its own ingested_at (= avail of its transaction, durable_ordering.commit_instant).

revision_policy.same_item_different_body_hash: EventRevisions are keyed per (source item, content hash). A hash without a revision gets one only when an observation carrying it concludes IN_SCOPE_V1; otherwise no revision is invented and snapshot_binding exposes the newer unnormalized content. A hash that already has a revision reuses it (A-B-A).
revision_policy.same_item_same_body_hash: same content revision; NO duplicate revision created
revision_policy.unchanged_refetch: still raw-first with auditable observation metadata; no duplicate normalized revision

scope.broad_domain: Federal Reserve monetary-policy press-release content (the discovery surface)
explicitly_out_of_scope: all other Federal Reserve press releases
scope.honest_statement: This provider V1 does NOT claim to cover every possible FOMC action or communication. It positively classifies exactly one release pattern, and every absence claim it makes is scoped to that pattern.
in_scope: FOMC monetary-policy statements published as official Federal Reserve press releases AND matching the frozen positive predicate
scope.taxonomy_note: the frozen rev4 taxonomy type is retained; capture_scope_id records that V1 captures a deterministic SUB-FAMILY of it
scope.v1_target_subset: official items satisfying the frozen positive FOMC-statement predicate
scope.why_narrow: first EventStore proof; one event family, deterministic, causally honest, offline-replayable

security_requirements: redirect destinations validated before being followed
automatic client redirect following forbidden; manual redirect loop with per-hop validation, grant and deadline
decoded HTTP body size bounded incrementally during production (feed 2 MiB, statement 5 MiB)
60-second activity-independent total deadline per physical attempt covering DNS, TCP, TLS, write, headers, body and content decoding
no cookies as a correctness dependency
custom XML entity declarations unsupported, so no internal entity-expansion path exists
XML parser filesystem and resource resolution forbidden
no second-pass entity or XInclude expansion

NOTE: the decoded-body caps bound parser INPUT only; XML parser expansion safety comes from the DOCTYPE/XInclude prohibitions above, never from the size caps. "XXE disabled" alone is NOT a sufficient summary of this list.
no ambient proxy inheritance or auto-discovery for provider requests (http_policy.proxy_policy)

algorithm: 1. O_latest = the item's latest (by commit_seq) PROCESSABLE primary record within P(T), any mode and clock verdict; H = its body hash
2. E_latest = the item's latest CLOCK_VERIFIED PROCESSABLE primary record within P(T)
3. if an integrity diagnostic for O_latest exists within P(T): CURRENT_CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_NEWER_UNNORMALIZED_SOURCE (corrupt newest source; never a fallback)
4. else if O_latest is CLOCK_VERIFIED and an IN_SCOPE_V1 EventRevision of the item with hash H and a CLOCK_VERIFIED link exist within P(T): CURRENT_REVISION with that revision (A-B-A reuse)
5. else if O_latest is not CLOCK_VERIFIED, E_latest exists with hash H, and an IN_SCOPE_V1 revision with hash H and a CLOCK_VERIFIED link exist within P(T): CURRENT_REVISION with that revision

6. else if the item has any IN_SCOPE_V1 EventRevision within P(T): CURRENT_CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_NEWER_UNNORMALIZED_SOURCE, exposing O_latest's id, mode, clock verdict and its processing outcome within P(T) (or pending)
7. else if O_latest is CLOCK_VERIFIED and its processing outcome within P(T) is DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE: NOT_IN_V1_SCOPE
8. else if O_latest exists or the item is outstanding within P(T): SOURCE_ACTIVITY_NO_REVISION
snapshot_binding.availability_evidence: a CURRENT_REVISION carries its CAUSALLY_ADMISSIBLE_BOUNDED observation-to-revision links within P(T) with mode, observed_at and avail; strict causal consumers require a LIVE_ELIGIBLE link (design backfill_policy)
snapshot_binding.binds: normatively overrides design rev4 revision_policy.selection and extends snapshot_identity.binds (identity_binding) for FOMC source items in events_as_of(T) and InformationSnapshot(as_of=T); all other design snapshot rules (mode, read consistency, fail-closed) still apply
snapshot_binding.discovery_state: under FOMC_RESOLVED the read exposes discovery from F, the latest PROCESSABLE LIVE feed record within P(T): if F is cycle-starting and its conclusion is within P(T), that conclusion (EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO or NOT_ZERO, with cycle_id and B); if F is not cycle-starting (not LIVE_ELIGIBLE, LATE_EVIDENCE included), NO_CURRENT_CYCLE; if F is not FEED_RECORD_TERMINAL within P(T) or its conclusion is outside P(T), DISCOVERY_PENDING. EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO is exposed only as F's own conclusion; an older conclusion is never presented as current
snapshot_binding.identity_binding: declared override of design rev4 snapshot_identity.binds: an FOMC snapshot's identity additionally binds the selection policy id FOMC_CURRENT_CONTENT_SELECTION_V1, the read horizon H, the provider-level read_state, the discovery_state and, per FOMC item, its selection state (algorithm step and state name), O_latest's record id, the current revision id if any, the exposed link ids and step-6 processing outcome, and the LIVE-availability state; two snapshots that differ in any of these never share an identity
snapshot_binding.live_watermark: the FOMC part of a read is admissible only if the store view up to H contains a transaction W with resolved avail > T and no UNRESOLVED transaction precedes W (a SNAPSHOT_WATERMARK transaction may be committed); otherwise the read's FOMC state is FOMC_CAUSAL_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED (read_state). Other providers' content is unaffected. Replay at the same (T, H) gives the same result, resolved or not.
snapshot_binding.mode: DURABLE_OBSERVED (RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE never admits FOMC V1 content because source_available_at is null)
snapshot_binding.mode_scope: content selection considers every PROCESSABLE record of every mode and verdict within P(T); current content requires a CLOCK_VERIFIED record; LIVE availability requires LIVE_ELIGIBLE; unverified raw is unresolved source state (barrier)
snapshot_binding.no_masquerade: consumers asking only for usable normalized events receive nothing current for the barrier states (steps 3 and 6), together with the explicit state; an older revision is never presented as current and source activity is never presented as absence
snapshot_binding.ordering_authority: commit_seq only; never revision creation time, content hash order or wall timestamps
snapshot_binding.prefix: P(T) = the longest commit_seq prefix in which every transaction has a resolved avail <= T (causal_predicates.avail). An UNRESOLVED transaction ends the prefix: visibility waits there while capture continues. Every snapshot input (records, processing outcomes, revisions, links, diagnostics) is read only within P(T); anything outside P(T) does not exist for the read. Reads use one consistent store view.
snapshot_binding.qualifying_observation: availability evidence: a CAUSALLY_ADMISSIBLE_BOUNDED record within P(T); LIVE availability requires a LIVE_ELIGIBLE one
snapshot_binding.read_horizon: every read is evaluated over one consistent store view whose horizon H is the largest commit_seq it contains; H is persisted with the snapshot and bound into its identity. avail, P(T), the watermark and every input are computed only from records with commit_seq <= H. A resolved avail never changes when H grows, so replay with the same (T, H) reproduces the live read exactly, including a FOMC_CAUSAL_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED result (design replay_policy exact replay).
snapshot_binding.read_state: every events_as_of(T)/InformationSnapshot(T) read carries one provider-level FOMC state: FOMC_RESOLVED when live_watermark holds, FOMC_CAUSAL_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED otherwise, and FOMC_NOT_ADMISSIBLE_IN_MODE for RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE reads. Under any state other than FOMC_RESOLVED no FOMC item state, cycle or zero conclusion, revision or FOMC source-health state is exposed, whether or not any FOMC item would be listed; an empty FOMC part is never presented as resolved
snapshot_binding.replay: the same (T, H) gives the same states and the same snapshot identity offline
snapshot_binding.strict_consumers: a consumer requiring LIVE availability receives, for a CURRENT_REVISION, nothing current plus CURRENT_REVISION_NOT_LIVE_AVAILABLE unless the item's latest LIVE_ELIGIBLE primary record within P(T) carries the current revision's hash (a return to older content seen only through backfill or unverified records is never LIVE-available)
snapshot_binding.ties: commit_seq is a total order over transactions and every per-response or outcome record has its own transaction; P(T) is a prefix

failure_classification_v1.commit_failure: normalization/EventRevision commit failure after durable raw keeps the existing mapping (no ingested_at, no EventRevision visibility), never becomes EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO, and blocks zero for the affected cycle.
failure_classification_v1.first_failure_wins: The processing order is: validation, FIX15 admission, transport, status gate, bounded body production, durable persistence, collector clock check, media type, charset/UTF-8, XML security, XML syntax, feed structure, HTML title/date anchors, classification, normalization, commit. The first failing stage determines the state and later stages do not run. Concurrent limits during the network phase are ordered by which occurred first.
failure_classification_v1.logical_fetch_result: A logical fetch's health result is the outcome of its last physical attempt, recorded on the fetched surface (discovery_feed or primary_statement). A reobservation failure is recorded on primary_statement and never marks the feed or the provider globally unavailable.
failure_classification_v1.missingness: Every failure state is missingness; none is evidence of zero events (source_health.never).

order: RAW_CORRUPTION (NO_PROVIDER_HEALTH_STATE + CORRUPTION_FAIL_CLOSED)
LOCAL_PERSISTENCE_FAILURE (NO_PROVIDER_HEALTH_STATE)
CLOCK_UNVERIFIED (NO_PROVIDER_HEALTH_STATE)
SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (transport, deadline, redirect, status, truncation, content-coding)
PARSER_FAILED (size, Content-Type, charset, UTF-8, XML security/syntax, feed structure, title/date anchors)
no failure state (successful check, including healthy negatives, conflicts and non-gating diagnostics)
precedence.rule: when several conditions apply to one response or record, the recorded state is the first applicable entry of this ordered list

failure_classification_v1.rate_limited_state: RATE_LIMITED ('client ceiling reached') is only a non-failure diagnostic meaning work waited for FIX15 admission. It is never SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, PARSER_FAILED or EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO, never fails or satisfies an obligation, and is not a discovery cycle. Whether and how often such diagnostic records are written affects no traffic, observation, revision, obligation, zero or replay decision (rate_limiter.wait_semantics).
failure_classification_v1.redirect_target_failures: An attempted redirect target that fails at transport, deadline or status maps exactly as the same failure on an initial request.
failure_classification_v1.rule: Every failure maps through source_health.mappings to exactly one existing rev4 state or NO_PROVIDER_HEALTH_STATE; overlaps are resolved only by failure_classification_v1.precedence. No new global state is added.
failure_classification_v1.successful_check: a successful non-zero feed or primary check records no failure state; its cycle conclusion or processing outcome is the success record

mappings.classification conflict (exactly one of: no failure state: CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT outcome, outstanding relevant item

source_health.scope_note: a feed outage must NOT mark all Federal Reserve data globally unavailable
source_health.state_reuse_note: PARSER_FAILED is used only for actual inability to process required syntax. Classification outcomes (DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE, CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT, UNSUPPORTED_DISCOVERY_SHAPE) are not health failures; unresolved ones block zero through OUTSTANDING_RELEVANT_ITEM_V1. No sixth global state is invented: a successful check records no failure state.
source_health.status_states_note: one existing state covers every HTTP status and redirect failure: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No per-status health state is introduced.
source_health.vocabulary: design rev4 missingness_policy states only; no new global state invented

structured_economic_extraction: DEFERRED - not required to identify the statement family; belongs to a later enrichment phase

backfill_manifest.health: per-entry outcomes are recorded on primary_statement with observation_mode HISTORICAL_BACKFILL; a manifest run never asserts EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO
backfill_manifest.max_entries: 1000 raw array entries, counted before deduplication
backfill_manifest.order: ascending lowercase-hex source_item_id, independent of operator order
backfill_manifest.per_entry_work: one HISTORICAL_BACKFILL episode per entry per manifest record (retry_policy)

canonical_serialization.binding: the existing repo primitive scripts/trading_lab/market_data_store.py::_canonical_timestamp: a timezone-aware instant converted to UTC and serialized with Python datetime.isoformat(), i.e. 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00' or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff+00:00' when the microsecond field is non-zero
canonical_serialization.case_notation: timestamps written with a 'Z' suffix in adversarial cases are notation for UTC instants, not the persisted serialization
canonical_serialization.comparison: All ordering, equality and arithmetic use parsed timezone-aware instants. Lexical comparison of timestamp strings is FORBIDDEN.
canonical_serialization.determinism: the same instant always serializes to the same string; revision identity inputs that include timestamps use this serialization
canonical_serialization.precision: the resolution of that primitive (Python datetime, microseconds). No truncation, rounding or widening beyond what the primitive represents; no separate FOMC precision regime.

collector_clock_check.design_binding: design rev4 clock_anomaly_policy (collector clock anomaly: flag, degrade or fail closed; never rewrite one timestamp from another)
collector_clock_check.independence: the per-response check uses only that response's own receipt reading and Date/Age; no record inherits clock trust (causal_predicates.constants.CLOCK_REFERENCE_MAX_AGE_S)
collector_clock_check.inputs: the response's own persisted wall_at_receipt and final-response Date/Age field lines only
collector_clock_check.late_evidence: a LATE_EVIDENCE record (retry_policy.attempt_outcome_fence) is treated as CLOCK_UNVERIFIED by every rule, whatever its own check says
collector_clock_check.persisted: wall_at_receipt, Date and Age field lines, verdict
collector_clock_check.replay: the verdict is recomputed from the persisted response fields alone and must equal the recorded verdict; a mismatch or missing input fails replay closed
collector_clock_check.rule: Each admitted complete final-200 response is checked on its own: it is CLOCK_VERIFIED iff its final response carries a usable clock reference (timestamps.http_clock_header_parser, Age <= 86400) and |wall_at_receipt - (Date + Age)| <= causal_predicates.constants.CLOCK_CHECK_TOLERANCE_S. Otherwise it is CLOCK_UNVERIFIED.

unverified_effects.health: NO_PROVIDER_HEALTH_STATE with a durable CLOCK_UNVERIFIED diagnostic
unverified_effects.processing: processed to a terminal local outcome if PROCESSABLE (causal_predicates.PROCESSABLE); outcomes are non-causal

content_source_available_at.design_compatibility: design rev4 already supports a null source_available_at bounded by observed_at; NO new design primitive is introduced

declared_release_at.what_it_does_NOT_establish: that the currently observed body bytes existed, or were public, at that instant

age.occurrences: zero lines means Age = 0; two or more make the clock reference INVALID
age.range: 0..2147483647 accepted as a number; larger is INVALID

date.whitespace: optional whitespace around the field value is trimmed; inside the value the IMF-fixdate spacing is exact

http_clock_header_parser.invalid_effect: clock_reference_usable = false; the content itself is not rejected on that ground

release_time.timezone_inference: FORBIDDEN - the abbreviation is read from the document, never derived from the date

zone_label_policy.optional_diagnostic: An implementation MAY attach a NON-CAUSAL diagnostic noting a seasonally unusual label. It is not required, never alters declared_release_at, never substitutes an offset, never rejects, is not a replay input, and its presence or absence is non-material.
zone_label_policy.replay: Conversion depends only on persisted body bytes, the frozen literal table and this CaptureSpec hash; no timezone database or platform locale.
zone_label_policy.rule: EST means exactly UTC-05:00 and EDT means exactly UTC-04:00, by the printed label alone, irrespective of calendar date or season. The parser follows the explicit source label and never corrects it.
